When the film or show arrives, whoever requested it gets a Your request is ready notification on their iPhone or iPad, if notifications are on for that profile. See Notifications and widgets. To follow a request while it downloads, use Seerr itself, or Coming soon in Flexarr's sidebar for what Sonarr and Radarr are expecting. #If requests don't work Discover has no Seerr rows: check Seerr shows a green dot in Settings › Connections. If it says it can't be reached, or the API key isn't right, edit it there. "Requests need a Seerr server": Seerr isn't connected yet. "This profile can't request films" (or shows): that kind of library is hidden from the profile you're using. "Seerr didn't accept the request": it may already be requested, or Seerr turned it down. Seerr's own requests page says why. #Audiobooks Book requests arrive in the next release, on the web only. Seerr doesn't handle books, so Flexarr asks Readarr, Bookshelf or Chaptarr itself. Connect one in Settings › Connections, then under Requests in Settings › Libraries switch on Book requests (preview) and choose its Quality, Metadata and Folder. Note Book requests are a preview, off to start with. Bookshelf, the Readarr fork most people run, can't always search by title: its searches go to Goodreads, which often doesn't answer. Typing a book's ISBN works better. Coming soon, new books arriving and deleting through the app work whether requests are on or not. In Discover's search, Search for any film, show or book, find a book you don't have and choose Request. Each result says whether it's In your library, Requested or available to request. Flexarr adds the book (and its author, if they're new, without following their other books), then asks for it to be found. When it arrives, whoever asked hears that it's ready to listen. With more than one audiobooks library, the main profile chooses where each profile's books go with New books go to, in the profile's editor in Settings › Profiles.

title: Finding things
description: Home and its rows, search, Discover, collections, Coming soon, genres, library order and Continue Watching.
text: The ways into your libraries, beyond opening one. #Home Home opens on Continue watching, then rows such as Ready from your watchlist, your favourite Live TV channels, the latest unwatched films and shows, Top 10 films in your library, Because you watched…, genre rows that change each day, and Coming soon. The rows come from your server, so every app shows the same ones in the same order. Each profile chooses its own in Settings › Home & browse on the web: turn a row on or off, and drag it to move it. The same page sets the rows of each film and TV library's Browse, a music library's rows and the shelves of an audiobooks library's front page. Profiles that were there before keep the rows they had; a new profile starts with a shorter Home (the music rows other than Made for you, New audiobooks, Continue listening kept apart and Highly rated films start off) that it can add to. Kids profiles always have the standard Home and menu. With more than one film or TV library (say Films and Films in 4K), Combine libraries of the same kind gives Home one Latest unwatched row for all your film libraries and one for all your TV ones. It's on to start with. On a new server, Home on the web shows Finish setting up with the steps you skipped in the setup guide. Each opens the right page in Settings, and Hide puts the list away. #Search Web: Search at the top of every page, or press / or ⌘K (Ctrl-K on Windows). iPhone and iPad: the Search tab. Apple TV: Search in the sidebar. Before you type, search shows your recent searches and what you opened from them, so you can go back with one press. They follow your profile between devices. Remove one, or Clear them all. Search forgives typos, accents and punctuation: "breking bad" finds Breaking Bad, "amelie" finds Amélie and "spiderman" finds Spider-Man. That works for titles, albums, people and genres, and for titles you ask Siri for. With Seerr connected, the iPhone's Search also lists titles you don't have under Not in your library: add one to your watchlist or Request it. On the web and Apple TV, search for them in Discover. #Discover Discover is on the web and the Apple TV. With Seerr connected, it has rows of films and shows from beyond your library: Trending this week, Popular films, Popular new shows and Coming to cinemas, and For you, from Trakt if you've connected Trakt. Its search box finds any film or show, to add to your watchlist or request. Below the rows, Your library by genre has a tile for each genre in your libraries. Profiles with an age limit don't see Discover or Coming soon, since Flexarr can't tell how old a title it hasn't got is for. #Collections Collections is in the web app's sidebar, under Browse. It has: Yours: collections only you see. For everyone: the household's, made by the main profile. Franchises: film series from Radarr, once you have two of their films. Choose New collection to make one: either Titles I choose, or a smart collection whose titles match rules (a genre, years, a rating, watched or not, and more) and keep themselves up to date. Suggested has ideas from what's in your library. Add a title to a collection from its ⋯ menu with Add to collection…. Show on Home puts a collection on Home, in every app. Trakt lists you choose in Settings › Trakt show here too, just for you. Kids profiles don't have Collections. #Coming soon Coming soon, in the web app's sidebar, lists what Sonarr and Radarr expect over the next few weeks, day by day, with what's downloading now at the top. Home has a Coming soon row too. #Genres Film and TV libraries have a Genres view: a tile for each genre, with a picture from one of its titles, that opens the library's titles in that genre. Web: Genres beside Browse and All films (or All shows) at the top of the library. iPhone and iPad: choose Genres at the top of the library. Apple TV: Genres in the switch at the top of the library. To have libraries open on another view, choose it in Settings › Libraries. #Library order Put your libraries in the order you like, and every app follows it. Each profile has its own order. Web: Settings › Navigation. Drag a library, or use the arrows. Apple TV: Settings › Sidebar. iPhone and iPad: Settings › Library order. Drag a library by its handle. Podcasts and Live TV are in the list too. Under Browse on the same web page, turn off what you don't use: Watchlist, Collections, Playlists, Live TV, Discover and Coming soon. They leave the menu in every app that has them, for your profile only, and still open from Home and links. Hiding isn't a restriction: to keep something from a child, use a kids profile or an age limit. #Continue Watching Continue watching on Home holds what you're part way through and the next episode of shows you're watching. A poster's menu (press and hold it in the apps) has two ways to tidy it: Mark as unwatched, on anything you're part way through, forgets your place without marking it watched. It leaves the row and starts from the beginning next time. Remove from Continue Watching, on a show's next episode, takes the show out of the row until you play another episode. Mark as watched is there too, for something you finished elsewhere.

title: Playback and transcoding
description: How Flexarr plays a file as it is, repackages it, or converts it, and how to set up hardware acceleration on your server.
headings: Three ways a file can play
Direct play: the file as it is
text: Every time you press Play, Flexarr works out the least it has to do for that screen to show the file. Most of the time that's nothing at all. This page explains the three ways a file can reach you, what your server needs for the hardest of them, and how to see which one is happening. #Three ways a file can play #Direct play: the file as it is When a device can open the file and decode its picture and sound, Flexarr sends the file untouched. The server does no more work than a file share would. This is the best case: full quality, and the lightest load on the server. On Apple TV, iPhone and iPad, Play files directly is on by default. With it, the app opens almost any file itself, including MKV and AVI files and AV1, VC-1, MPEG-2 and XviD video, decoding in software what the hardware can't. HDR and Dolby Vision stay as they are. The server only steps in for the few files the app can't open. #Repackaging: same picture, new wrapping Sometimes the picture is fine but the file around it isn't. A typical case is an MKV with H.264 or HEVC video, when Play files directly is off. Flexarr then copies the original picture into a stream the device accepts, cut at the file's own keyframes. Nothing is re-encoded, so you lose no quality, HDR and Dolby Vision included, and the server barely notices. Starting and seeking stay instant. MKV files can be repackaged straight away. Other files are indexed in the background the first time they're played, and repackage from the next time. #Transcoding: converting as it plays When the device can't decode the picture, or the stream has to be smaller, Flexarr converts the file as you watch, to H.264 video. It converts only what you're about to watch, so you can still jump anywhere in a film instantly. HDR is converted to SDR on the way. Converting is real work for the server. By default it converts at most three videos at once. Beyond that, the player says the server is busy rather than slowing everyone down. #Hardware acceleration Converting video on the server's graphics chip is much faster and lighter than on its processor. Choose how in Settings › Streaming › Hardware acceleration. This page belongs to the main profile, the one that manages the server. Choice For Automatic (recommended) Apple VideoToolbox on a Mac. Anywhere else, Automatic means the processor, so pick one of the options below. Apple VideoToolbox Macs. Automatic already picks this. VA-API (Intel and AMD on Linux) Intel and AMD graphics on Linux. A VA-API device field appears, set to /dev/dri/renderD128 unless you change it. Intel Quick Sync Intel processors with built-in graphics. NVIDIA NVENC NVIDIA graphics cards. Off: convert on the CPU No graphics chip, or for troubleshooting. A Software speed choice appears. Only the options your server's copy of FFmpeg was built with are listed. On Linux, VA-API and Intel Quick Sync are listed only when the server can see a graphics device, so in Docker pass /dev/dri into the container. NVIDIA NVENC is listed whenever FFmpeg has it, even if the container can't reach the card. After changing this, play something that needs converting and check it starts (see How to tell what's happening, below). Note On a Mac, files whose video the graphics chip can't decode (old AVI and XviD files, VC-1) are decoded on the processor and still encoded on the graphics chip. You don't need to do anything. #Without a graphics chip With Off: convert on the CPU, Software speed offers Fastest, lowest quality, Fast (recommended) and Slower, better quality. Faster uses less of the server, at some cost to picture quality. Converting video in software is demanding. A recent multi-core desktop processor can usually keep up with a 1080p stream or two. A low-power NAS processor may struggle with even one, and converting 4K or HDR in software is heavy for almost anything. If your server has no graphics chip, the good news is that Apple devices rarely need converting at all, thanks to Play files directly and repackaging. #Limiting quality Settings › Streaming › Limit each stream to caps every stream from the server: No limit, 20 Mbps, 10 Mbps, 4 Mbps (good for remote viewing) or 2 Mbps. A file above the limit is converted down to fit. Use it when your home internet's upload is slow and people watch away from home. Bear in mind it applies to every stream, at home too, and anything converted to fit loses HDR and lossless sound. At home on a decent network, No limit is best. Note Live TV is different: away from home, channels automatically come in a reduced version. See Live TV and recording. In the web player, the quality button in the corner chooses Best for this device, 1080p, 720p or 480p for what you're watching now. #In the player Audio sync: when the sound and picture are out of step, open the player's audio menu (the Audio button, a waveform) and use Audio sync. Each press of − or + moves the sound 10 ms; hold one (a long press on the Apple TV remote) to move 50 ms at a time. It's saved for that file, for everyone in the household. Downloads play as they were made. Sleep timer: stop in 15, 30, 45 or 60 minutes, or at the end of the episode. In the last minute the picture dims and asks Still watching?. Any button adds 15 minutes (on iPhone, a tap or a shake). Otherwise the sound fades out and playback pauses. Speed: from 0.5× to 2×. A speed chosen during an episode is kept for the rest of the show, on every device. A film's is for this time only. Previous: a few seconds in, it starts the episode again. Press it again to go to the episode before. In a film, or a first episode, it starts again. The audio menu also has the soundtrack, and dialogue boost, night mode and speakers. Subtitles have a menu of their own: see Subtitles, skipping and Up Next. #Settings that are per device On Apple TV, iPhone and iPad, these live in the app's Settings › Playback under this device's own settings, not your profile's: Play files directly: on by default. Off, the server sends a stream instead and converts what the device can't play. Lossless surround: appears when Play files directly is on. See HDR and Dolby Atmos. Skip back and forward: 10, 15 or 30 seconds. Dialogue boost, Night mode and Speakers: appear when Play files directly is on. See HDR and Dolby Atmos. The web keeps them in Settings › Playback under Sound in this browser. #How to tell what's happening Web player: the quality button says Original when the file is playing as it is, and Auto when it's being repackaged or converted. Apple TV, iPhone and iPad: with the player's controls showing, a line in the corner describes the stream. It ends in "Original" for a file played as it is, says "repackaged" when the original picture is copied, and gives a size and bitrate (such as "1080p H.264 at 10 Mbps") when it's converted. Settings › Overview: under Watching now, each stream is tagged Original file or Converting to …. If something is converting that you didn't expect, check whether Limit each stream to is set, whether Play files directly is off on that device, and whether picture-based subtitles are on in the web player (they have to be burned into the picture). For more, see Troubleshooting.

title: HDR and Dolby Atmos
description: How Flexarr gets HDR10, HLG, Dolby Vision, Atmos and lossless surround to your Apple TV, and the Apple TV settings that matter.
headings: Set up the Apple TV first
Dolby Atmos in Dolby Digital Plus
TrueHD, DTS-HD Master Audio and PCM
text: If you have a 4K HDR television and a soundbar or receiver, you want the picture and sound to arrive as they are in the file. Flexarr is built to do that on Apple TV, without converting anything. This page explains what reaches your TV, and the few settings on the Apple TV itself that make the difference. Note The Apple TV app isn't on the App Store yet. Until it is, you can install it from Xcode. #Set up the Apple TV first These are Apple's own settings, in the Apple TV's Settings › Video and Audio. They matter more than anything in Flexarr. Format: set it to the best your television supports. Apple recommends 4K SDR (or 4K SDR 60Hz) when you turn on matching below, so menus look right and HDR switches on only for HDR films. Match Content › Match Dynamic Range: turn this on. The Apple TV then switches the television into HDR10, HLG or Dolby Vision to suit each film, and back again afterwards. Match Content › Match Frame Rate: turn this on too. Films shot at 24 frames a second then play at 24, without judder. Audio Format: leave this on its automatic setting so the Apple TV sends Dolby Atmos to equipment that takes it. If Atmos isn't showing on your soundbar or receiver, check here that Dolby Atmos is available. Flexarr follows Match Content: when it's on, the Apple TV switches mode for each title Flexarr plays. Tip Without Match Dynamic Range, an Apple TV set to a fixed Dolby Vision output has no HDR10 mode. A plain HDR10 film may then be converted to SDR when it reaches the Apple TV as a stream from the server. Turning on Match Dynamic Range avoids this. #HDR: what reaches your TV With Play files directly on (the default on Apple TV, iPhone and iPad), the Apple TV plays the file itself. HDR10, HLG and Dolby Vision reach the television untouched. With Play files directly off, the server repackages the original picture into a stream without re-encoding it. Here's what the television gets: In the file On the television HDR10 HDR10, as it is HLG HLG, as it is Dolby Vision profile 5 Dolby Vision, on a Dolby Vision television Dolby Vision profile 8.1 Dolby Vision on a Dolby Vision television, otherwise HDR10 Dolby Vision profile 7 (UHD Blu-ray) Its HDR10 base layer HDR10+ HDR10, with its HDR10+ scene-by-scene metadata kept for televisions that use it A film's details say HDR10+ when its file carries HDR10+, and Dolby Vision, HDR10+ when it has both. HDR is only converted to SDR when it has to be: when the television doesn't show HDR, when the stream is limited in size (see Limit each stream to in Playback and transcoding), or when the video itself has to be converted. On iPhone and iPad, HDR shows on screens that support it. #Sound: Atmos, TrueHD and DTS How the sound reaches your equipment depends on what's in the file. #Dolby Atmos in Dolby Digital Plus This is the kind of Atmos you'll find on most streaming-service releases. It reaches the Apple TV intact and signalled as Atmos, ready for an Atmos receiver, soundbar or HomePods. #TrueHD, DTS-HD Master Audio and PCM The Apple TV can't play these as they are, so Flexarr makes sure nothing is lost on the way. Play files directly on, Lossless surround on: the app decodes the soundtrack and sends it as multichannel PCM over HDMI. Use this with a receiver or an eARC soundbar that accepts it. Play files directly on, Lossless surround off: they're sent as Dolby Digital Plus, which any soundbar or receiver plays. Play files directly off: the server sends them as lossless FLAC, up to 7.1, instead of squeezing them into 5.1. Plain DTS is decoded with nothing more lost on the way. Note TrueHD soundtracks with Atmos currently play as lossless surround without Atmos's height channels. Keeping them is on the roadmap. #Lossless surround Lossless surround comes on by itself when the Apple TV is connected to a receiver or soundbar that takes it. To change it, open Flexarr's Settings › Playback on the Apple TV: it's under This Apple TV, while Play files directly is on. The iPhone and iPad app has the same switch, for AirPlay or a connected display. Turn it off if your television is plugged straight into a soundbar over ordinary ARC (not eARC), or if you hear nothing on TrueHD or DTS films with it on. #Dialogue boost and night mode The player's audio menu, and Settings › Playback, have three sound settings that each device keeps for itself: Dialogue boost (Low, Medium or High) raises the centre channel, where the voices are, and the speech frequencies. Night mode squeezes loud and quiet together, so explosions don't wake the house and whispers stay audible. On a schedule turns it on between set times, even in the middle of a film. Speakers folds the sound to Stereo or 5.1. Auto plays every channel your equipment takes; leave it there for headphones, so the iPhone's Spatial Audio gets the whole mix. On Apple TV and iPhone they need Play files directly. While any is on, Atmos plays without its height channels, so leave them off (and Speakers on Auto) for the full Atmos. Over AirPlay the sound plays as it is. The web has them too, for live TV as well, except in Safari. #Watching away from home With a quality limit set in Settings › Streaming, anything above it is converted down. Lossless sound becomes compressed and HDR becomes SDR, because neither fits through a small connection. See Away from home. #Other screens iPhone and iPad: surround is mixed down for headphones and the speakers, and passed on over AirPlay. Web browsers: fine for a quick watch, but use the Apple TV for HDR and surround. Live TV: channels that broadcast Dolby Digital or Dolby Digital Plus come through as 5.1 on Apple TV, iPhone and iPad at home. See Live TV and recording. #Checking what you're getting While something plays on the Apple TV, bring up the player's controls. The line in the corner says what's playing, for example "Original HEVC (Dolby Vision), repackaged, lossless FLAC 7.1 sound", or the resolution and sound followed by "Original" for a file played as it is. Your television's and receiver's own info screens confirm what they're receiving. If HDR or Atmos isn't coming through, check the Apple TV's Match Content and Audio Format settings first, then Troubleshooting.

title: Subtitles, skipping and Up Next
description: Subtitles of every kind, skipping intros, recaps and credits, the next-episode countdown and scrubbing previews.
headings: Skip buttons, or skipping by itself
text: Flexarr's own player on Apple TV, iPhone and iPad, and the web player, share the same features for subtitles and getting through a series. Your choices belong to your profile, so they follow you from the TV to your phone. #Subtitles #What Flexarr finds Flexarr picks up these kinds of subtitles: Embedded: tracks inside the video file, as most MKV files have. Closed captions carried inside the video itself, as American TV recordings have them. They're listed as CC. Flexarr checks for them when it scans a file. Sidecar files: .srt, .vtt, .ass or .ssa files beside the video, named after it. Add a language and, if you like, forced or sdh before the extension (cc, or hi after the language, as Bazarr writes it, also means SDH): Heat (1995).mkv Heat (1995).en.srt Heat (1995).en.sdh.srt Heat (1995).en.forced.srt Sonarr, Radarr and most subtitle tools name files this way already. Subtitles come as text (SRT, WebVTT, ASS and the like) or pictures (PGS from Blu-rays, VobSub from DVDs, DVB from broadcasts). Text subtitles are drawn by the player at the size you choose. Picture subtitles are drawn by the app on Apple TV, iPhone and iPad when Play files directly is on. In a web browser they have to be burned into the picture, which means the server converts the video while they're on. #Styled subtitles ASS and SSA subtitles, as most anime has, can carry their own fonts, colours, positions, signs and karaoke. The web player draws them exactly as they were made, with the fonts attached to the file. On Apple TV, iPhone and iPad they keep their colours and go where they were placed, such as a sign at the top of the picture, in your caption style's font. #Closed captions and teletext Closed captions carried inside the video, as American TV recordings have them, are listed as CC and work on every device. Flexarr looks for them when it scans a file. Teletext subtitles, as European TV recordings carry them, show on Apple TV, iPhone and iPad with Play files directly on. The subtitles menu there has a Teletext page choice for channels that don't use the usual page, such as 888 in the UK or 150 and 777 in Germany. In a web browser, teletext shows only when the server's FFmpeg can read it, as the Docker image's can; a server on a Mac can't. #Finding subtitles When a film or episode has no subtitles in your language, or the ones it has are out of time, Flexarr can fetch some through Bazarr. It works for what Sonarr and Radarr manage, in the languages Bazarr is set up for, and every profile but kids profiles can use it. In the player, open the subtitles menu and choose Search for subtitles…. On a title's page, it's under ⋯ on the web and Apple TV, and the Subtitles button on iPhone and iPad. Wait while Bazarr asks its subtitle sites. It can take a minute. Choose one and Download, or Pick the best for me. Those marked Matches your file were made for your exact copy, so they should be in time. The subtitles are saved beside the video, so every app sees them. In the player, the title carries on where it was with them on. Note Bazarr only searches for a film or show that has a languages profile. If it has none, the first search from Flexarr gives it Bazarr's first profile; for an episode, that's the whole show. From then on Bazarr looks after it like anything else with a profile, so if Bazarr is set to search for missing subtitles on a schedule, it will fetch them for that title by itself. To keep Bazarr to what you ask for, go to Settings › Scheduler in Bazarr and set Search for Missing Series Subtitles and Search for Missing Movies Subtitles to Never. If subtitles beside the video drift out of time, choose them, then Re-sync to audio. Bazarr lines them up with the soundtrack, which takes a minute or so, and the player picks up the new timing when it's done. For an offset that's the same all the way through, Timing in the subtitles menu is quicker. #Turning them on and off Choose a subtitle track, or Off, from the subtitles menu in the player. Flexarr remembers your choice for that film or show, so the next episode and the next sitting start the same way. That includes Off. The same goes for the audio track, chosen from the audio menu: pick another language once and the rest of the series follows. Forced subtitles, the ones that translate the odd line of foreign dialogue, come on by themselves when they match the soundtrack's language. They don't count as you choosing subtitles, so the full subtitles won't switch themselves on next time. #Size Choose Small, Standard, Large or Extra large in Settings › Playback › Subtitle size, or the player's subtitles menu. It's your profile's setting on every device. #Position Subtitles sit at the bottom of the picture. If they cover text in the picture, or your TV cuts off its edges, choose Raised, Higher or Top under Subtitle position. With Subtitles in the black bars on, films wider than the screen get their subtitles in the black bar below the picture instead of over it, whenever they fit there. Both are your profile's settings on every device, in Settings › Playback and the player's subtitles menu. Styled subtitles that place themselves keep their own places. #Timing If subtitles come too early or too late, choose Timing in the player's subtitles menu and move them to match the speech: a quarter of a second at a time on the web, or from half a second to two seconds on Apple TV, iPhone and iPad. Each film or episode remembers its own timing. On Apple devices, Timing isn't offered for a download, for subtitles burned into the picture, or when Play files directly is on and the file plays as it is. For the last of these, turning Play files directly off brings Timing back. #Skipping intros, recaps and credits #How Flexarr finds them Flexarr looks for intros, recaps and credits in two ways: Chapter names. If a file has chapters called "Intro", "Opening", "Recap", "Previously" or "Credits", Flexarr uses them. This is the only way it finds recaps, and the only way it finds credits in films. Audio fingerprinting. For episodes without useful chapters, Flexarr listens to each episode of a season and compares it with the episodes either side. A theme tune and credits music repeat while everything else changes, so the shared stretch is the intro or the credits. A season needs at least two episodes for this to work. Opening credits early in an episode count as an intro to skip, not as the end of the episode. #When markers are ready The analysis runs in the background while the server is quiet, a season at a time. When someone starts watching a season that hasn't been analysed yet, that season jumps the queue, so skipping is usually ready by the next episode. Settings › Overview shows how far it has got under Background work. The player's timeline shades the intro and credits once they're known. #Skip buttons, or skipping by itself By default, a Skip Intro or Skip Recap button appears when one starts. On iPhone and Apple TV it shows by itself, without the rest of the controls. To skip without pressing anything, turn these on in Settings › Playback on any device, or from the player's menu on the web: Skip intros: jumps past the opening titles. Skip recaps: jumps past "Previously on…". Skip credits: ends the episode as the credits start, rather than when they end. They're your profile's own, on every device. #Up Next When the credits start, a Next Episode card offers the next one. For a show with no credits found, it comes a little before the end instead: up to two minutes for an hour-long episode. When the episode ends, a five-second countdown starts the next one. Press Cancel to stop it. Flexarr gets the next episode ready while the credits play, so it starts straight away. If the server is busy with other people's streams, it starts the usual way instead. Turn the countdown off with Auto-play the next episode in Settings › Playback: the player then closes when the episode ends, or as the credits start with Skip credits on. If you watch a special in the middle of a season, Up Next carries on with the regular episodes afterwards. When you're shuffling a show, the countdown plays another random episode. The player also has previous and next episode buttons: see In the player. #Scrubbing previews Drag along the timeline and small pictures show where you'll land. Flexarr makes these the first time a file is played, so on a film's very first viewing they may not be there yet. On Apple TV, hold the left or right of the remote's touch surface to scan at 2×. Each further click doubles the speed, up to 16×. The other side turns it round, and Select lands.

title: Music
description: Music libraries with Lidarr's artwork and details, a queue, playlists, lyrics, daily mixes, artist radio and offline albums.
text: Flexarr plays your music library like a streaming app: artists with their pictures, albums on shelves, a queue, playlists and lyrics. It's at its fullest in the web app, with the Apple apps covering everyday listening. #Setting up a music library In Settings › Libraries, choose Add library, pick Music and point it at your music folder. If you use Lidarr, connect it in Settings › Connections. See Connect your *arrs. Lidarr isn't required, but it makes a big difference. With it, artists and albums take their names, years, descriptions and artwork from Lidarr: the artist's own picture rather than an album cover, and a cover for every album even when the files carry none. An artist's page shelves releases into Albums, EPs and singles, Live and compilations and Other. Without Lidarr, Flexarr reads everything from the files' tags. A track by someone other than the album's artist, such as a duet or a compilation track, shows its own artist. Compilations without an album artist are filed under Various Artists. #Playing and the queue Every artist, album and playlist has Play and Shuffle, which open Now Playing. An artist's Play runs through their whole catalogue, oldest album first. Picking a single song leaves you on the list. On the web, the now-playing bar stays with you as you browse. Click its cover for Now Playing across the whole window: a big cover, the controls and what's up next, with light in the cover's colours moving with the music. Escape closes it. Tracks and albums have Play next and Add to queue in their menus. The queue panel above the bar lets you drag tracks into order, remove them, clear the lot or skip to any track. The queue and your place in it survive a page reload. On Apple TV, iPhone and iPad, the player has next and previous, seeking, shuffle and repeat, and shows the whole queue. Music carries on while you browse, and playing a film pauses it until you're done. #Now Playing on Apple TV While music plays, a Now Playing entry appears in the sidebar, with the cover, controls and the queue, and a bar along the bottom of the screen that goes away a few seconds after the music is paused. Play/pause on the remote works from anywhere in the app. Stop ends the music and takes the bar and Now Playing away until you play something else. Behind Now Playing, light in the cover's colours moves in time with the music. Turn it off with Settings › Playback › Music visualiser. #On iPhone and iPad A mini-player sits above the tab bar. Tap it for the full Now Playing sheet, with the cover, scrubber, controls, queue and AirPlay. The lock screen, Control Center and a paired Apple Watch control playback too. #Playlists Each profile has its own playlists. On the web, choose Add to playlist from a track's, album's or artist's menu, and manage them from the Playlists page: rename, reorder by dragging, or delete. Playlists play on Apple TV, iPhone and iPad as well, and appear in a Your playlists row on Home. Making and editing playlists is on the web for now. #Lyrics Flexarr shows lyrics on the web, Apple TV, iPhone and iPad. On the web, they're in a Lyrics panel under the album's track list. In the apps, there's a Lyrics button on Now Playing. Timed lyrics follow the song with the current line lit, and choosing a line jumps there. Flexarr doesn't fetch lyrics from the internet. It reads them from your files, in this order: An .lrc file beside the track, with the same name (timed lyrics). Lyrics stored in the track's own tags. A .txt file beside the track, with the same name. Brothers in Arms/01 - So Far Away.flac Brothers in Arms/01 - So Far Away.lrc Any tool that saves .lrc files next to your music works. #Made for you, and radio These are on the web for now. Daily mixes: up to four for each profile, built from what it plays, grouping artists who share genres ("Rock Mix"). About 40 tracks each, the same all day and fresh tomorrow. They appear once a profile has played twenty or so tracks, in a Made for you row on Home and in a music library's Browse view. Artist radio: start it from an artist's page. It's a station of about fifty tracks from that artist and others sharing their genres. Home rows: Recently played, Most played, More from artists you play and New albums. Move them or turn them off in Settings › Home & browse. #Gapless, crossfade and volume The web player loads the next track before the current one ends, so the switch between them takes a few milliseconds. Live albums and DJ mixes flow on almost without a gap. In the web app, Settings › Playback › Music in this browser has three more: Crossfade: Off, or fade the next track in over 2 to 12 seconds as the current one ends. Normalise volume: on by default. It uses ReplayGain (and Opus R128) tags in your files to level loudness, so a quiet album and a loud one play at about the same volume. Tracks without these tags play as they are; a tagging tool can add them. Visualiser: the moving light behind Now Playing. These are kept per browser, since speakers and taste differ by room. #Albums offline On iPhone and iPad, every album and playlist has a Download button. Tracks the phone plays as they are (AAC, ALAC, MP3, FLAC, WAV and AIFF) are kept as they are. Anything else is converted to AAC. Downloaded tracks carry a green arrow and play with no connection. See Downloads.

title: Podcasts
description: Follow podcasts from Apple's directory or any feed, with Up Next, speeds, a sleep timer, offline episodes on iPhone and iPad, and OPML import.
headings: The episodes folder on the server
text: Podcasts are built into Flexarr. There's no library to add and nothing to set up: they sit with your libraries, and each profile follows its own shows. They're on the web, iPhone and iPad. They aren't on the Apple TV, and kids profiles don't have them. #Finding shows Open Podcasts and choose Browse. Top charts, by category, come from Apple's podcast directory. Search finds any show in that directory. A feed's address works too: paste it into the search box to add a show Apple doesn't list, such as a private or members-only feed. Whose charts you see is set by the main profile in Settings › Libraries, under Podcasts › Charts and search. It starts as the server's own region. #Following a show Choose Follow on a show. It joins the row of shows you follow on the Podcasts page, and its newest episodes you haven't heard appear there and in a New podcasts row on Home. Flexarr checks feeds by itself, more often for shows that publish often. On a show's page: Unplayed episodes come first. Newest first or Oldest first sets the order. Oldest first suits shows heard in order, and Play then starts the oldest you haven't heard. A show you follow remembers its order. Mark all as played clears a back catalogue in one go. #Listening Episodes play in the same bar as music, and pick up where you left off on any device. Skip back and forward by your profile's steps (30 seconds each to start with), on screen, on the lock screen and with headphones. Smart rewind starts a little earlier after a pause. Speeds from 0.8× to 3×. Changing it in the player changes your profile's speed, which books share. Sleep timer (the moon): stop after a set time, or at the end of the episode. Notes swaps the cover for the episode's notes and chapters. The chapter playing shows above the scrubber, with arrows to the next and the last. Now Playing says when the episode will end, at the speed it's playing. When an episode ends, the show's next one plays, or else the newest you haven't heard. Episodes play through your server rather than straight from the podcast's host. That means they work away from home over Tailscale as they do at home, and podcast hosts don't see where each listener is. #Up Next Up Next is your own queue of episodes, shared between the web and your phone. Use Play next or Add to Up Next on any episode. Reorder or remove episodes on the Podcasts page, or in Now Playing on iPhone and iPad. An episode leaves Up Next once it starts playing. Episodes you're part way through also show on Home, in Continue watching or listening, on the web, iPhone, iPad and Android. To leave them out, turn off Books and podcasts in Continue watching in Settings › Podcasts & audiobooks (on the web it's in Settings › Home & browse, and on the Apple TV in Settings › Playback). #Settings Podcast settings belong to each profile, and are in Settings › Podcasts & audiobooks on the web, iPhone, iPad and Android: Speed, Skip back, Skip forward and Smart rewind, shared with audiobooks. Books and podcasts in Continue watching (on the web, in Settings › Home & browse). Download new episodes and how many of each show's newest to keep, for phones and tablets. On the web, Show in the sidebar is in Settings › Navigation. Home's New podcasts row can be moved or switched off in Settings › Home & browse. #Offline on iPhone and iPad Download any episode to listen with no connection. Or turn on Download new episodes in Settings › Podcasts & audiobooks: the newest unplayed episodes of every show you follow then download by themselves. Episodes you deleted yourself are never downloaded again by themselves. A downloaded episode is deleted once you've heard it to the end or marked it played, whether you downloaded it or the app did. One finished on another device, such as the web, goes the next time the app catches up with the server. Automatic downloads wait for Wi-Fi, unless you turn off Automatic downloads on Wi-Fi only in Settings › Downloads. They never use Low Data Mode. An episode you download by hand comes over mobile data too. What you hear offline counts once you're back online. #The episodes folder on the server To reach your phone, an episode is first fetched to your server, then the phone takes it and the server deletes its copy. It waits in the Podcasts Episodes folder, in Settings › Libraries. This starts as a folder in Flexarr's own data folder. If that's on a small drive, choose Change and pick a folder on your media drive instead. #Bringing your shows over Most podcast apps can export the shows you follow as an OPML file. In Flexarr on the web, use Import on the Podcasts page and choose that file. Export gives you an OPML file of your shows to take elsewhere. #Notifications and widgets On iPhone and iPad, Flexarr can tell you when a show you follow has a new episode, with buttons to play or download it. Turn this on in Settings › Notifications. There are widgets for Continue listening and Up Next too. See Notifications and widgets. #Siri Siri plays podcasts on iPhone and iPad: "Play The Rest Is History in Flexarr" plays the episode you'd hear next. "Play the latest …", "What's new in my podcasts", "Add … to Up Next" and "Play my Up Next" work too. See Siri and Shortcuts. #CarPlay The iPhone app has a CarPlay view for podcasts, with Up Next, new episodes and your shows, plus speed and skips. It switches on once Apple approves Flexarr for CarPlay, which hasn't happened yet.

title: Audiobooks
description: An audiobooks library with chapters, series, authors and narrators, a player with speed, smart rewind, a sleep timer and bookmarks, and books on your phone offline.
text: Note Audiobooks arrive in the next release of Flexarr. Audiobooks are a library like films, TV and music. Flexarr finds the books in your folders, reads their chapters and details, and plays each book as one, however many files it has. Readarr, Bookshelf or Chaptarr can fetch books for it, but they don't have to: a folder of audiobooks is enough. Books are on the web, iPhone, iPad and the Apple TV. Kids profiles don't see them. #Adding the library In Settings › Libraries, add a library, choose Audiobooks, and pick the folder your books are in. Flexarr reads these layouts: Author/Title/… a folder of files is one book Author/Series/1 - Title/… series and number from the folders Author/Series/Vol. 1.5 - 2004 - Title {Narrator}/ Author/Title/CD1/…, CD2/… disc folders are parts of one book Author/Title.m4b single-file books side by side Author - Title [B0DPXK6Y7B].m4b an Audible id in the name Files: m4b, m4a, mp3, aac, flac, ogg, opus and wma. Books protected by Audible (.aax, .aaxc) can't be played: Library health lists them. Order: files play by disc, then track number, then name, with numbers in names counted as numbers. Details: Flexarr reads them from files beside the book first (metadata.opf from Readarr, Bookshelf or Calibre, Audiobookshelf's metadata.json, desc.txt, reader.txt, a cover image), then the files' tags, then the folder names. It never changes your files. Chapters come from the files themselves, a .cue sheet, or one per file. A long book in a single file with none is split into half-hour parts. #Finding books The library's front page has Continue listening, Next in series, Recently added, your series and authors, and what you've finished. All books lists every book, with filters for what you haven't started, are part way through or have finished, and by narrator, length and language. Genres, Series and Authors list those; pick a genre to see its books. Books you're part way through also show on Home, in Continue watching or listening with your films, shows and podcast episodes. To keep them in their own Continue listening row instead, turn off Books and podcasts in Continue watching in Settings › Podcasts & audiobooks (on the web it's in Settings › Home & browse, and on the Apple TV in Settings › Playback). A book's page shows its series ("Book 3 of 7"), authors and narrators, how long it is and how long is left at your speed, its chapters, and more in the series, by the author and read by the narrator. A series' page lists its books in order with the next one to hear picked out. Home can show Continue listening, Next in series and New audiobooks: each profile turns them on or off in Settings › Home & browse on the web. #Listening Speed goes from 0.5× to 3.5×. Each book remembers its own; new books start at your default. Skip back and forward by the steps you choose. Headphones, the lock screen and the car use them too. Smart rewind: after a pause, a book starts a little earlier, more the longer you were away. Sleep timer: after some minutes or at the end of the chapter. On a phone, shake it to add time. Bookmarks, with a note if you like, are on the book's page and in the player. Finished: a book counts as finished in its last two minutes or last 2%, whichever comes first, or when you choose Mark finished on its page. Start over goes back to the beginning and keeps the record. Part-way through a book, it asks first. Mark as unread forgets your place and that you finished it, as if you'd never started. Across devices: your place is saved as you listen. If another device got further, the player offers to jump there. At the end of a book in a series, the player offers the next one. In the player, the seek bar covers the chapter playing; switch it to Book to see the whole book. Time left counts at your speed. Set your default speed, skip steps and smart rewind in Settings › Podcasts & audiobooks on the web, iPhone, iPad or Android, or Settings › Playback on the Apple TV. They're your profile's, on every device, and podcasts share them. A book you've set a speed for in the player keeps its own. #On your phone Download a book on iPhone or iPad to listen without a connection. Your place is sent when you're back online. In Settings › Downloads, Download the next book in a series fetches the next one when you finish a book, and Remove books once finished deletes a book when you've heard it. Both are off to start with. See Downloads. The Continue listening widget and "Resume listening in Flexarr" with Siri pick up the book you're on. CarPlay will list books too, once Apple approves Flexarr for CarPlay. #Details from the internet When a book's files leave gaps, Flexarr fills them from Audible (through the community-run Audnexus service), Open Library, and if you add keys, Google Books and Hardcover. The main profile chooses the Audible store under Audiobook details in the web app's Settings › Libraries; Google Books and Hardcover turn on once their key or token is saved there. Audible's chapters replace guessed ones when they match the book's length. On the web, the main profile can change a book's chapters: open its page, choose ⋯ › Edit chapters…, rename them or Shift all by a few seconds, then Save. Use Audible's fills them in; Save keeps them. ⋯ › Fix match… finds the right book when Flexarr picked the wrong one. To fix a book's details yourself, choose ⋯ › Edit… (it asks for the admin PIN): change its title, authors, narrators, series, genres, description or year. Locked keeps your changes when the library is scanned again. Genres that only say it's an audiobook, such as Audiobook or Spoken Word, are left out. #Author photos Each author gets a photo and a short biography. Flexarr looks first for an author.jpg or folder.jpg in the author's folder, then asks Readarr, Audible and Open Library, and tries again later for anyone still missing one. A picture in the author's folder wins over anything found online. If an author has the wrong photo or biography, open their page in the web app and choose Edit (it asks for the admin PIN): pick another photo, upload your own, or rewrite the biography. Your changes stay put. Turn off Locked to let Flexarr fill in anything that's missing. #Readarr, Bookshelf and Chaptarr Connect any of them in Settings › Connections as Readarr / Bookshelf / Chaptarr. Bookshelf keeps one kind of book per instance, so connect the one for audiobooks. With one connected: New books show up as soon as they're imported. Their details and covers fill what your files don't say. Coming soon lists books on their way from authors you follow. Deleting a book in Flexarr deletes it there too, and it isn't fetched again. You can request books from the web app, a preview you switch on in Settings › Libraries: see Requests.

title: Watchlist
description: Keep a list of films and shows to watch later, whether you have them yet or not, and hear when they arrive.
text: Each profile has its own watchlist: films and shows you want to watch later, whether they're in your library yet or not. When something on it arrives, you hear about it, and it waits on Home under Ready from your watchlist. Kids profiles don't have a watchlist. #Adding and removing Where How Web app Watchlist on a title's page, the bookmark under a poster in Discover and search, or Add to watchlist in a poster's menu. iPhone and iPad Watchlist on a film's or show's page, Add to watchlist when you press and hold a poster, or tap a title under Not in your library in Search. Apple TV Watchlist on a title's page (Discover's too), or Add to watchlist when you press and hold a poster. Siri "Save Severance in Flexarr" for a title in your library, or "Add to my watchlist in Flexarr" and then say any title, whether you have it yet or not. Assistants Ask an assistant connected over MCP to add or remove a title, even one you don't have yet. Choose On watchlist on its page to take a title off again, or Remove from watchlist when you press and hold its poster (on the web, the bookmark on its card). Adding a title twice keeps one, and adding one you took off brings it back. Titles leave the list by themselves once you've dealt with them: a film when you've watched it, a show when you've started it (it carries on in Continue watching). A title you've seen before stays until you watch it again. #Your watchlist On the web, Watchlist is in the sidebar under Browse. On iPhone and iPad it's at the top of Libraries, and on the Apple TV it's in the sidebar beside Discover. The iPhone has a Watchlist widget too (see Notifications and widgets). Each title says where it's got to: You see What it means Its usual poster It's in your library. Play it. On its way It's been requested, or Sonarr or Radarr are getting it. Out and a date It isn't released yet. Request It's out, but nobody's asked for it. Choose Request to add it to your library (see Requests). A title you don't have also says which streaming services it's on, such as On Netflix, for the country set as Streaming Region in Seerr. Every app can show only one kind (Ready to watch, On its way, Coming or Not available), only films or only shows, and sort the list: Ready first (the default), Recently added, Release date (newest first) or Title. Titles you don't have yet need Seerr connected (see Requests). Without it, you can still keep a watchlist of what's in your library. #When something arrives When a title on your watchlist arrives in your library, your iPhone or iPad says From your watchlist, if that profile has notifications on. It follows the Requests switch in the app's notification settings. If you also requested the title, you hear once, as Your request is ready. See Notifications and widgets. #Requesting what you add The main profile can have a profile's watchlist request what it adds: open Settings › Profiles, edit the profile, and turn on Request what … adds to the watchlist. It's off to start with, and only shows when Seerr is connected and the profile has no age limit. With it on, a film or show that isn't in your library and hasn't been asked for is requested as soon as it's added. It never requests: titles that are already in your library or already requested films for a profile that can't see any film library, or shows for one that can't see any TV library titles brought across from another service rather than added in Flexarr Taking a title off the watchlist doesn't cancel its request.

title: Trakt
description: Keep what you watch, where you're up to and your watchlist in step with Trakt, both ways.
text: Connect a profile to your Trakt account and Flexarr keeps the two in step: what you watch, where you're up to, and your watchlist. Each profile connects its own account, and nothing is shared until that person connects. #Connecting Open Settings › Trakt in the web app, on iPhone or iPad, or on the Apple TV. Choose Connect. Flexarr shows a code. On any phone or computer, go to trakt.tv/activate and enter the code. On a TV, scan the QR code to open that page on your phone. On iPhone, Copy code and open Trakt copies the code and opens the page; on the web, Copy code. You don't need to wait on that screen: your server waits for the code for 10 minutes. Once you've entered it, Settings › Trakt shows your Trakt name. A Trakt account can be connected to one profile only, so nothing is counted twice. #Bringing your history across Once you're connected, Bring your Trakt history across shows you what would change before anything does (See what changes on the web). For example: Trakt has 12 films and 340 episodes. 200 are here, 41 not yet watched in Flexarr. Choose Bring across to go ahead. Anything watched on Trakt is marked watched in Flexarr, with the date you watched it. Anything watched in Flexarr that Trakt doesn't have goes to Trakt. Titles you've watched that aren't on your server yet are remembered. When one arrives, it's already marked watched. Nothing is ever marked unwatched, on either side. It's offered once. When it's done, Settings says History brought across; after that, everything stays in step by itself. To bring it across again, disconnect and connect again. #Staying in step After that, it all happens by itself: What How Watching Trakt shows what you're watching while it plays. When Flexarr counts a film or episode as watched (near the end, or once the end credits start), so does Trakt. Marking watched Mark as watched in Flexarr goes to Trakt, and so does anything you watched on a download away from the server. Watched elsewhere Plays in other apps connected to Trakt come to Flexarr within a few minutes. Where you're up to Stop part way and Trakt keeps your place. Stop in another app connected to Trakt, and Flexarr picks up from there. Your watchlist Add or remove a title in either place, and it's added or removed in the other. Titles that come from Trakt are never requested by themselves; they show Request if they're not here. Marking something unwatched in Flexarr leaves Trakt as it is: your Trakt history stays true, and Flexarr won't mark it watched again. Sync now in Settings › Trakt checks straight away rather than waiting (once a minute at most). Everything a connected profile watches goes to Trakt, whichever library it's in, and Trakt profiles are public unless you make yours private on trakt.tv. #Lists and picks Lists: in Settings › Trakt, choose any of your Trakt lists, or ones you've liked, and each shows up in Collections on the web, just for you, kept in step with Trakt. Titles on the list that are here show as usual. Films that aren't here show with Request. For you, from Trakt: once you're connected, Discover on the web and Apple TV has a row of Trakt's picks for you, with titles you have first and ones you've watched left out. #If something's wrong You see What to do Trakt signed Flexarr out You revoked Flexarr on trakt.tv, or it wasn't used for months. Choose Connect again; your history stays. Trakt's watchlist is full A free Trakt account holds a limited number of titles. New titles stay on Flexarr's watchlist; make room on Trakt and they'll go across. Waiting to send Trakt or your internet is down. Flexarr keeps the changes and sends them when it can. No Trakt in Settings, or Trakt isn't available on this server. on the web Kids profiles don't have Trakt. Otherwise, your server can't reach Flexarr's Trakt service. Check it can reach the internet. Disconnect in Settings › Trakt stops it all and makes Trakt forget Flexarr. What you've watched stays as it is, in both places. Making a profile a kids profile, or removing it, disconnects it too. Backups include each profile's Trakt sign-in. Restoring an older backup may mean connecting again, as Trakt replaces a sign-in each time it's renewed. #Your own Trakt app Flexarr uses its own Trakt app, so there's nothing to set up. If you'd rather use your own (Trakt only lets VIP members create one), the main profile can enter its Client ID and Client secret in Settings › Connections › Trakt. Everyone then connects again, as sign-ins belong to the app that gave them.

title: Downloads
description: Keep films, episodes, albums, playlists and podcasts on your iPhone or iPad to watch and listen with no connection.
text: The iPhone and iPad app can keep films, episodes, albums, playlists and podcast episodes on the device, for a flight, a train or anywhere without a signal. In the next release, audiobooks too. #Downloading something Tap the download button on a film's or episode's page, on an album or playlist, or on a podcast episode. It starts straight away, at the size you chose (see Picture size). The button shows how it's going: An hourglass, "Getting ready": your server is preparing it. Wi-Fi: it's waiting for Wi-Fi. A filling ring: it's coming down to the device. Podcast episodes show the ring from the start. A green arrow: it's ready to play with no connection. (A tick means watched or played.) An exclamation mark: it failed. Tap it to see why, and to Try again. Tap the button while a download is under way, or once it's here, to remove it. Downloads carry on with the app closed, and pick up where they left off if the connection drops or the phone locks. Everything you've downloaded is in the Downloads tab, where it plays with Skip Intro and the countdown to the next episode as usual. #What your server does first Your server gets each download ready before it's sent, one at a time. It converts a film or episode to a size and format the phone plays, or sends it as it is when it can. It does this quietly in the background and waits while anyone is watching something that's being converted, so a download never slows someone's film down. A prepared download that isn't collected within a week is deleted from the server. #Picture size Choose the size once, in the app's Settings › Downloads › Size: Automatic (720p): the default. Looks good on a phone and doesn't take much space. Sound is stereo. Original: the full picture and sound, but takes the most space. A title whose original won't play on the phone comes at 1080p instead. Small (480p): the least space, for a long trip on a small phone. Text subtitles come with the download. Picture-based subtitles (from Blu-rays and DVDs) don't. Albums, playlists and podcasts come as their files are when the phone can play them: AAC, ALAC, MP3, FLAC, WAV and AIFF. Anything else is converted to AAC. #Automatic downloads In Settings › Downloads: Download the next episode: on by default. Once you've downloaded an episode, the next one downloads too. Episodes are deleted a day after you finish them. Automatic downloads on Wi-Fi only: on by default. Downloads the app starts by itself, like the next episode or new podcast episodes, wait for Wi-Fi. Turn this off to let them use mobile data too. In the next release, two more for audiobooks, both off to start with: Download the next book in a series: when you finish a book, the next one in its series downloads. Remove books once finished: a book is deleted once you've heard it. Automatic downloads never use Low Data Mode. Downloads you start yourself use mobile data as well as Wi-Fi. For podcasts, Download new episodes in Settings › Podcasts & audiobooks keeps the newest unplayed episodes of every show you follow on the device. See Podcasts. #Storage Settings › Downloads shows the space your downloads use, under Storage, and has Delete all downloads. To remove one thing, tap its download button and remove it. A podcast episode you delete is never downloaded again by itself. A podcast episode is deleted as soon as you've heard it to the end or marked it played, here or on another device. Signing out of the server on the device deletes its downloads. #Watch progress What you watch and hear offline is sent to your server when the device is back online. Resume points, watched ticks and Continue Watching then catch up on every other screen. #Two devices on one profile An iPhone and an iPad on the same profile each get their own copy of a download. New podcast episodes download by themselves on both. #Downloading away from home Downloads work away from home over Tailscale as well as at home. A big Original download over a slow home upload can take a while, so it's best started at home on Wi-Fi.

title: Your iPhone as a remote
description: Control what's playing on your Apple TV from your iPhone or iPad: pause, scrub, skip the intro, change subtitles and sound, pick another episode, and carry on watching on the phone.
text: When an Apple TV in your home is playing something from Flexarr, the iPhone and iPad apps show a Playing on TV bar above the tabs. It shows the TVs playing for the profile chosen on the phone, so each person sees their own: Claire's film on the bedroom TV doesn't show on Dan's phone. There's nothing to set up: the TV and the phone only need to be signed in to the same server, with the TV's Flexarr app open. The bar has play/pause. Tap it for the remote. The × hides the bar until that TV plays a different show or film; it doesn't stop anything, so it's safe while someone else is watching. #The remote Scrubber: drag to anywhere in the film or episode. Underneath is how far in it is, how long is left and when it ends. Back and forward 10 seconds, and previous and next episode. Previous starts the episode again, or goes to the one before if you're near the start. Skip Intro, Skip Recap and Next Episode appear here whenever the TV shows them. Audio and subtitles, speed and sound (dialogue boost, night mode and speakers). Subtitles are lit while they're on, speed while it isn't 1×, and sound while any of it is changed. Continue on iPhone (Continue on iPad on an iPad) stops the film or episode on the TV and carries on from the same moment on your phone. The TV goes back to the title's page and says it's now playing on your phone, by name. Stop stops it on the TV. For a few seconds you can Undo, which starts it again from where it stopped. Episodes lists the season: tap one to play it on the TV. A title from a library hidden from your profile shows as playing but not what it is. You can pause, skip and stop it, but not continue it on your phone, undo a stop, or change its tracks or sound. With more than one TV playing, tap the TV's name at the top to switch between them. For the TV's menus and its volume, use the Remote in Control Center, as before. If a button doesn't work (the TV has gone to sleep, or its Flexarr app is closed), the phone says why. Note A few buttons need the TV's Flexarr app to be up to date, and the phone only shows the ones it can do. If the phone is signed in with the server's key rather than as its own device, the bar can take up to half a minute to catch up with changes made on the TV. #On the Lock Screen While the remote is following a TV, your phone shows what's playing on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island, with back 10 seconds, play/pause and forward 10. Tap it to open the remote. It keeps up while the phone is locked, as long as notifications are on for your server. To keep the title private, your phone puts the title and picture there itself. Only whether it's paused, how far in it is, how long it is and its speed travel through Flexarr's notification service, because Apple reads these updates directly and they can't be encrypted like notifications. Anyone holding your locked phone can pause or skip the TV from it, as with any Lock Screen controls. To turn it off, go to Settings › Flexarr › Live Activities on the phone. Swiping it away hides it for that title.

title: Live TV and recording
description: Watch TV channels in Flexarr with a guide, favourites and rewind, and record programmes and series, using Dispatcharr as the source.
text: Flexarr can show TV channels next to your films and shows, with a programme guide, favourites, pause and rewind, and recording. It doesn't come with any channels. You bring your own, through Dispatcharr. Live TV is on the web, Apple TV, iPhone and iPad. Kids profiles don't have it, and a profile with an age limit sees only the channels the main profile picks under Channels for kids in Settings › Live TV. #What you need Flexarr reads channels and their guide from Dispatcharr, a free, self-hosted app that gathers TV sources into one channel list. Dispatcharr is the only source Flexarr supports. You can't give Flexarr an M3U playlist or XMLTV guide address directly; add them to Dispatcharr instead. Into Dispatcharr you can bring: Your own tuner, such as an HDHomeRun on an aerial or cable connection, for free-to-air channels. An IPTV service you're entitled to use, given to Dispatcharr as an M3U playlist with an XMLTV guide. Setting up Dispatcharr itself is covered in its own documentation. Once it has channels and a guide, carry on below. Important Only use sources you have the right to watch. Flexarr doesn't provide, find or recommend channels. #Connecting Dispatcharr First, in Dispatcharr: Add a user for Flexarr, at Streamer level. Give it a long, random XC password. This works as Flexarr's key. It can only list and play channels, never sign in to Dispatcharr or change anything. Give that user the channels you want in Flexarr. Then in Flexarr, as the main profile: Open Settings › Connections and edit Dispatcharr. Fill in Address (for example http://localhost:9191), User name and Key (XC password). Choose Test. It should say how many channels it found and how many connections your source allows at a time. Then choose Save. The channels and guide come in straight away. The guide refreshes every six hours, and channels you add or remove in Dispatcharr show up within five minutes. Refresh channels and guide fetches them now. Channel logos come from a community logo collection where it has a match, and from Dispatcharr where it doesn't. #Watching Live TV sits with your libraries. On the web, On now lists every channel with what's on, how far through it is and what's next, filtered by group. The Guide shows the next six hours, or up to a day, as a grid. On Apple TV, the guide has categories down the left and channels with three hours across. What's on now plays; anything later shows what it is. On iPhone and iPad, Live TV is a list of channels. The Guide button turns it into a grid, and List goes back. In the player, previous and next change channel. The Channels button lists every channel over the picture, with Last watched at the top so flipping between two is one press. On Apple TV, the Guide button opens the guide over the picture while the channel carries on behind it. Home has a Live TV row too, starting with the channel you watched last, then your favourites. #Favourites Star the channels you watch most. Each profile has its own, and Live TV opens on them. Web: select the star on a channel. Apple TV: press and hold a channel or programme. iPhone and iPad: swipe right on a channel, or press and hold. #Pause and rewind You can pause a channel and rewind it. The timeline shows the time of day, LIVE or how far behind you are, and a button to jump back to live. The server keeps the rewind window while anyone is watching a channel, so you can rewind to when the channel was first put on, up to the limit. Set the limit in Settings › Live TV › Rewind up to, from 15 minutes to 4 hours (1 hour to start with). It takes about 2 GB of space an hour for HD. #Picture and sound Channels that are already H.264 play as they come. Others (interlaced, MPEG-2 and HEVC) are converted, and interlaced channels are made smooth at 50 frames a second. On Apple TV, iPhone and iPad at home, channels broadcasting Dolby Digital or Dolby Digital Plus come through as 5.1. The web player is stereo. One channel is shared by everyone watching it, so a source that allows one connection can still serve the whole house. #Watching away from home Away from home, over Tailscale or the internet, channels come in a reduced version: at most 720p at about 2.5 Mbps, in stereo, so they keep playing on hotel Wi-Fi or a phone's data. At home they play as they come. Someone at home and someone away can watch the same channel at once. #Recording #Setting a recording In the guide, choose a programme (on Apple TV, press and hold it), then: Record for this showing, or Record series for every showing. On the web you can choose On any channel and New episodes only. A programme set to record has a red dot, and one a series covers has two. While it's recording it shows a REC badge. Live TV › Recordings lists what's coming up, the series being recorded (keep all of them or only the latest few), what's been recorded, and why anything didn't record. #Where recordings go Recordings are saved as MKV files, with the picture and every soundtrack as they came, nothing converted. They're named like TV episodes, for example Show/Season 2/Show - S02E05 - Episode.mkv, or by date when the guide doesn't number them. By default they go in a DVR folder at the top of the drive your TV library is on. To choose another, set Folder in Settings › Live TV. Recordings play like anything else in Flexarr, with resume and Continue Watching, from Live TV › Recordings. #Recording settings In Settings › Live TV: Start early and Run on: broadcasts drift, so recordings start a minute early and run five minutes on unless you change them. Keep free on the drive: no new recording starts with less than this free (100 GB to start with). The Recordings list says when that's why. Channels at once: how many channels can be open together, for watching and recording combined. As Dispatcharr says uses the limit your source reports. #When channels run out Watching and recording share your source's connections. Watching and recording the same channel counts once. A recording takes priority: if someone is watching another channel when it's due, that channel stops with a message. If every connection is recording, choosing another channel tells you what's recording and offers to watch that instead, or stop the recording. Recordings that would need more connections than you have are flagged as clashing when you set them. A recording under way when Flexarr restarts carries on afterwards.

title: Profiles
description: Give everyone in the house their own Continue Watching, history and settings, with an optional PIN, and choose which libraries each profile sees.
headings: What each profile keeps to itself
Choosing which libraries a profile sees
Letting things through, or keeping them out
text: A profile is one person's view of Flexarr. Everyone in the household can have their own, so your half-watched film doesn't turn up in someone else's Continue Watching, and their cartoons don't fill your "Because you watched" row. #What each profile keeps to itself Each profile has its own: Continue Watching, watched history and Up Next Playback settings: auto-play the next episode, skip intros, recaps and credits, and subtitle size. These follow the profile to every device, the Apple TV included. Watchlist, and its own Trakt account Podcasts: the shows it follows, its Up Next queue and its podcast settings Audiobooks (in the next release): where it is in each book, its bookmarks and its listening settings Music: playlists, daily mixes, and recently and most played Collections of its own (the main profile can also make collections for the whole household) Live TV favourites and the channel it watched last Recent searches, which follow it from device to device Libraries: which ones it can see at all (see below), and the order they're listed in Requests: which library what it asks for goes to, when you have two TV or film libraries A picture, a name and a colour Things that belong to the server, such as your libraries, connections to Sonarr, Radarr and Lidarr, and the layout of Home, are the same for everyone. #The main profile The first profile, made when you set Flexarr up, is the main profile. It manages the server, and it has a crown beside its name in Settings › Profiles and on its picture when you choose who's watching. Only the main profile can: change the server's settings, libraries and connections add, edit and remove profiles connect new devices, and see or replace the API key fix a wrong match, or delete a title through Sonarr or Radarr make and change the household's collections allow or block a title for kids, analyse a title, or scan a library for changes Every other profile can browse, watch, listen, make requests through Seerr, and open Settings to change its own settings: playback, podcasts, the sidebar's order, Trakt and where its requests go. #Unlocking settings Flexarr has an admin PIN: you choose it when you set Flexarr up. It belongs to the server, apart from the main profile's own PIN (see PINs). Watching as the main profile doesn't need it, and nor does tidying the library from a title's or library's page (the last three things above). Changing the server's settings, profiles and devices does. Open Settings on the main profile and the server's pages say Settings are locked: enter the admin PIN and choose Unlock. Settings stay unlocked on that browser or device for 15 minutes after your last change. They lock again sooner if someone else is chosen there, if you choose Lock settings at the bottom of the list, or if the server restarts. Being on your home network doesn't skip the admin PIN. A device asking to connect still shows up on the main profile while settings are locked. Choosing Allow asks for the admin PIN first. If there's no admin PIN yet (a server set up before Flexarr asked for one), Settings asks you to choose one before anything else. To keep the main profile's watch history private, give it a PIN of its own in Settings › Profiles, as for anyone. Choosing it then asks for that PIN; the admin PIN works there too. #Adding a profile On the web, signed in as the main profile: Go to Settings › Profiles and choose Add a profile. Give it a name, and if you like a picture and a colour. Choose Add a PIN if it should be private. Switch off any libraries it shouldn't see. Choose Add profile. If you bring your history over from Plex, your Plex Home profile pictures can come too. See Import from Plex. #PINs A PIN is 4 to 8 digits. Without one, anyone can switch to that profile. With one, Flexarr asks for it whenever someone chooses the profile. The main profile's PIN works like anyone's: add it, change it or remove it in Settings › Profiles. It can be the same as the admin PIN or different. The admin PIN is in Settings › Security. It can be changed but not removed, and changing it takes the current one. If you've forgotten it, see I forgot a profile's PIN. Without a PIN of its own, the main profile is chosen freely on browsers and devices you signed in. Someone coming in over Tailscale with their own account, or a browser at home that isn't signed in while there are kids profiles, is asked for the admin PIN instead, even when the main profile has a PIN of its own. Forgotten a profile's PIN? Choose Forgot PIN? under its PIN pad and enter the admin PIN: the PIN comes off, and you can give it a new one in Settings › Profiles. On a server from before the two were apart, the PIN you had became the admin PIN. The main profile kept it as its own too only if Ask for the PIN when someone chooses the main profile was on. Changing the admin PIN later doesn't change that one: change it in Settings › Profiles too. Wrong guesses lock out the device doing the guessing for a while, longer each time. Someone else guessing can't lock you out of your own profile. When wrong guesses at the admin PIN, or at the main profile's own, lock someone out, Flexarr notes it in its log and tells the main profile's phones (with notifications on), naming the device. #Choosing which libraries a profile sees When you have more than one library, each profile has a switch for each. A library that's switched off is hidden everywhere on that profile: Home, search, Discover, Coming soon and requests. Podcasts can be left out the same way. #Age limits and kids profiles #Age limits Any profile except the main one can have an age limit, in Settings › Profiles: U, PG, 12, 15 or 18. Titles rated above it are hidden from that profile on every device: Home, the libraries, search, Continue Watching, the next episode, collections, Siri and notifications. Opening one by its link says it isn't there. Ratings from any country count. An age is rounded up to the next UK step, so Germany's 16 counts as 18, and a few have a UK equivalent: PG-13 is 12, TV-14 is 15, and R and TV-MA are 18. A rating with its reasons ("Rated R for violence") counts by its first word. A show's seasons and episodes follow the show. An age limit decides what a profile sees, not who can leave it: anyone can switch to another profile, with no PIN but that profile's own. To keep a child on kids profiles, turn on Child lock. A profile with an age limit: doesn't see titles without a rating, or music and home videos, which have none doesn't see Discover or Coming soon, can't make requests and can't add podcasts, since Flexarr can't tell the age of a title it hasn't got sees clean podcasts, but not episodes marked explicit sees only the Live TV channels you pick, and no recordings #Letting things through, or keeping them out A whole library: switch on Fine for kids under it in Settings › Libraries. Everything in it shows, rated or not. Good for a folder of cartoons or family videos. One film or show: on its page, choose ⋯ then Allow for kids or Block for kids. Block wins even in a library that's fine for kids. Live TV: switch channels on under Channels for kids in Settings › Live TV. Until you pick some, a profile with an age limit doesn't see Live TV. #Kids profiles Switch on Kids profile for a child's profile (it comes on by itself for a new profile limited to U or PG). A kids profile: has no Settings, and no signing out on the web has no Podcasts, Watchlist, Collections, Live TV, Trakt or subtitle search (nor, from the next release, audiobooks) has no scores, no score-ranked rows such as Top 10, and a Watch again row on Home for the films and shows they've finished; on the web, bigger artwork too can't mark things watched, and has no trailers Setting one up needs an admin PIN. #Child lock For the playroom TV or a child's tablet, turn on Child lock, so only kids profiles can be chosen on that device: Web: the profile menu, then Child lock. Apple TV: Settings › Profiles, or press and hold a kids profile in the profile picker. iPhone and iPad: Settings, under Watching as, or hold the padlock on a kids profile's picture in the profile picker: child lock goes on with that profile. Turning it on from the main profile takes no PIN (from any other profile, the admin PIN). To turn it off, hold the padlock in the profile picker (on Apple TV, press and hold the kids profile), or choose Turn off child lock in the web's profile menu, and enter the admin PIN. You can also turn it off for any device from Settings › Security on the web, which marks those with Child lock on. Deleting the kids profile a device with child lock is on moves that device to another kids profile. If it was the last one, turn off child lock first. Note Child lock needs the device's own sign-in: a browser signed in with the API key once, or an app connected with a code. An app still connected with the API key itself is the server, so kids profiles can't hold a child there at all: connect it again with a code. With Only away from home in Settings › Security, a browser at home that hasn't chosen a profile starts on a kids profile, and choosing the main profile there takes the admin PIN.
