Giving it signs that browser in, so it doesn't ask again: turn on Child lock on a browser children share. #Who's watching when Flexarr opens When a household has more than one profile, Flexarr asks who's watching the first time a browser or device connects, and remembers the answer. #On the web The page is called Choose a profile. Profiles with a PIN say Needs a PIN. To switch later, open the menu under your profile picture at the top right and choose Switch profile. With two profiles, it says Switch to and the other person's name, and switches straight away unless that profile has a PIN. #On iPhone and iPad Tap your picture on Home, or go to Settings and tap Switch beside your profile. #On Apple TV Who's watching is at the top of the sidebar, with your profile picture. Select it to switch. A profile with a PIN asks for it on an on-screen keypad. An Apple TV in a shared living room can ask every time Flexarr opens, rather than opening as whoever watched last: Open Settings › Profiles on the Apple TV. Under When Flexarr opens, choose Ask who's watching. Profiles with a PIN then ask for it every time too. #Notifications and profiles An iPhone or iPad gets notifications for one profile: whichever it was on when notifications were turned on. Switching profile on the phone doesn't change that, though Settings › Notifications offers to move them to the profile you're on now. While child lock is on, they follow the phone to the kids profile, and go back when it's turned off. See Notifications and widgets.

title: Watch away from home
description: Reach your Flexarr server from anywhere with Tailscale, with no ports opened on your router, or through an HTTPS reverse proxy.
text: At home, your devices find Flexarr on the Wi-Fi. Away from home, they need a safe way back to it. The easiest is Tailscale, and it's the one Flexarr is built around. If you already run an HTTPS reverse proxy, that works too. #Tailscale Tailscale is a free app that puts your devices on a small private network of their own, called a tailnet. Your phone can then reach your server from a hotel or a train as if it were at home. The connection is encrypted, and nothing is opened on your router, so Flexarr isn't on the public internet. #Set it up On the server, install Tailscale from tailscale.com/download and sign in. In Flexarr on the web, signed in as the main profile, go to Settings › Remote access. Under Away from home, Tailscale should say Off. Connected as and your server's name. Choose Turn on. Flexarr shows its Private address, something like https://your-server.your-tailnet.ts.net:8443. It's HTTPS, with a real certificate from Tailscale. On your iPhone or iPad, install Tailscale from the App Store and sign in with the same account. Leave it connected. Open the Flexarr app once while you're at home, so it learns the private address. From then on, the iPhone, iPad and Apple TV apps switch by themselves. When the home address doesn't answer, they use the Tailscale one, and they go back to the home address when you're home again. There's nothing to change in the apps. In a browser away from home, open the private address instead of the usual one. Note The Mac app (coming to the Mac App Store) can't turn Tailscale on. Install Tailscale on that Mac and sign in, and Settings › Remote access shows the Mac's own Tailscale address to use. Note Flexarr needs the tailscale command on the same computer it runs on to turn this on. In Docker it can't see the Tailscale installed around it, so Settings › Remote access says Not available in Docker. To use Flexarr away from home from Docker, put it behind an HTTPS reverse proxy, or run Flexarr without Docker on a computer with Tailscale. #Who can get in When you first turn it on, your own Tailscale account is linked to the main profile. Anyone else you invite to your tailnet appears under People with their own Tailscale in Settings › Remote access. Choose a profile for each person. Anyone set to Not allowed is turned away, even though Tailscale lets them reach the server. Over Tailscale, watching works as it does at home. Someone whose account is linked to another profile can only choose the main profile with the admin PIN, even if the main profile has a PIN of its own. That browser then stays signed in until it's signed out, or left unused for two weeks. Changing settings asks for the admin PIN, as it does at home: see Unlocking settings. Don't use Tailscale Funnel for Flexarr. Funnel publishes an address to the whole internet. If Flexarr spots it, Settings warns you; turn remote access off and on again to make it private. #Quality away from home Hotel Wi-Fi and phone data are slower than your home network, and so is the upload speed of most home broadband. Live TV comes in a reduced version away from home: at most 720p, at about 2.5 Mbps, in stereo. At home, channels play as they come. Films and shows play as they do at home unless you set a limit. In Settings › Streaming, Limit each stream to caps every stream; 4 Mbps is a good choice for watching away. The limit applies at home too. On the web, the player's quality menu lets you choose 1080p, 720p or 480p for one viewing. On iPhone and iPad, downloading before you leave avoids the question altogether. See Downloads. #An HTTPS reverse proxy instead If you already run a reverse proxy such as nginx, Caddy or Traefik with an HTTPS certificate, you can put Flexarr behind it. If the proxy runs on another computer, or in Docker, tell Flexarr to believe the visitor addresses it passes on. Add it to trustedProxies in config.json, in the server's data folder, as a list of addresses or ranges: { "trustedProxies": ["172.17.0.1", "10.0.0.0/24"] } Without it, everyone who comes through that proxy counts as the internet and has to sign in. Restart Flexarr after editing; it's read at startup. If the proxy runs on the same computer as Flexarr, it must send X-Forwarded-For. In nginx: proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr; To be safe, also set this in config.json: { "loopbackNeedsForwarding": true } Then a request from the same computer that doesn't say who it's for counts as the internet, so a badly set up proxy can't let anyone in. A browser on the server itself then needs the API key too. Important In Settings › Security, Ask for it set to Only away from home lets devices on your home network in as the main profile without a key. With a reverse proxy, that makes the settings above matter. If in doubt, leave it on Always. #Why not forward a port? It's tempting to open port 8383 on your router and connect to http://your-home-address:8383. Please don't. Plain http:// isn't encrypted, so your API key, your sign-ins and what you watch cross the internet readable by anyone along the way. It also puts your server in front of every scanner on the internet. Plain http:// is fine on a home network you trust. Anywhere else, use Tailscale or HTTPS. #Connecting a device from outside Devices normally connect with a code you approve in Settings › Security › Connect a device, and that only works from your home network or over Tailscale. To connect an app through a reverse proxy instead, use the API key: iPhone and iPad: on the connect screen, choose Enter its address (under any servers it found, or once it has looked for a while), then Connecting from outside your home? Use an API key. Apple TV: Enter an address instead, then Connecting from outside your home? Use an API key. The API key is in Settings › Security under API key. Showing it asks for the admin PIN. It's also in config.json. Important The API key gives full control of your server. Don't paste it anywhere you wouldn't paste a password. If it leaks, Make a new key in Settings › Security replaces it, and can sign out every other browser and device at the same time.

title: Siri and Shortcuts
description: Ask Siri on your iPhone or iPad to play a film, the next episode of a show or a podcast, here or on your Apple TV, and build your own shortcuts.
headings: Siri on the Apple TV itself
text: Once the Flexarr app on your iPhone or iPad has signed in to your server, Siri understands it. There's nothing to set up. Siri learns the titles in your library when the app signs in, so it knows what you mean by "The Traitors" or "Heat". Every phrase needs the word Flexarr in it, so Siri knows which app you mean. #Things to say #Films and shows "Play the next episode of Curb Your Enthusiasm in Flexarr" "Play Heat in Flexarr" or "Watch Heat in Flexarr" "Shuffle Family Guy in Flexarr" "Continue watching in Flexarr" "Save Severance in Flexarr" for a title in your library, or "Add to my watchlist in Flexarr" and then any title (see Watchlist) A show plays the episode you're up to. A film carries on from where you left off. Shuffle plays a show's episodes in a random order, one after another. Continue watching picks up whatever you were in the middle of most recently. Don't say "Add Severance to my watchlist": iOS keeps that sentence for itself. #Podcasts "Play The Rest Is History in Flexarr" plays the episode you'd hear next "Play the latest The Rest Is History in Flexarr" plays the newest one you haven't heard "What's new in my podcasts in Flexarr" reads out the newest episodes, without opening anything "Add The Rest Is History to Up Next in Flexarr" "Play my Up Next in Flexarr", until the next release. From then on it's the Play Up Next action in the Shortcuts app. These work for podcasts the profile follows. See Podcasts. In the next release, "Resume listening in Flexarr" picks up the podcast episode or audiobook you heard last. #Controlling what's playing "Pause Flexarr", "Resume Flexarr", "Stop Flexarr" "Skip intro in Flexarr" "Next episode in Flexarr" "Skip back in Flexarr" and "Skip forward in Flexarr", 10 seconds at a time "Flexarr, turn on subtitles" and "Flexarr, turn off subtitles", said that way round, as Siri answers "Turn on subtitles" itself. Subtitles come on in your language where there are some. "Turn on night mode in Flexarr" (and "Turn off night mode in Flexarr"). If night mode is on a schedule and already doing what you asked, the schedule stays; otherwise Siri says it replaced the schedule. #Playing on your Apple TV By default, what you ask for plays on the iPhone or iPad you asked. To send it to an Apple TV instead: On the iPhone or iPad, open Flexarr and go to Settings › Siri. Under Siri plays on, choose the Apple TV. Now "Play the next episode of Severance in Flexarr" starts it on the TV, and Siri tells you where it's playing. Pausing, skipping, subtitles and night mode go to the same TV. You can also name a device as you ask, for example "… on the living room TV". The name is the one the device has in Flexarr's list of signed-in devices. Important The Apple TV only takes commands while Flexarr is open on it. If it isn't, Siri says so, and what you asked for starts if you open Flexarr on the TV within two minutes. Siri isn't limited to Apple TVs: any iPhone or iPad signed in to your server can be chosen in the same way, as long as Flexarr is open on it. #Siri on the Apple TV itself The Apple TV app carries the same actions for the Siri Remote, but it hasn't been confirmed that tvOS passes these requests to apps like Flexarr. For now, the dependable way is to ask your iPhone or iPad. #The Shortcuts app Everything Siri can do is also in the Shortcuts app on iPhone and iPad, as actions you can put together yourself or run from an automation. Search for Flexarr when adding an action. You'll find: Action What it does Play a film or show Plays a film, or the next episode of a show. Can start from the beginning. Shuffle a show Plays a show's episodes in a random order. Continue watching Picks up what you were in the middle of. Add to watchlist Puts a film or show from your library on your watchlist. Control playback Pauses, resumes or stops, skips the intro, moves on to the next episode, or skips back or forward. Subtitles Turns subtitles on or off. Night mode Turns night mode on or off, here or on another device with Flexarr open. Dialogue boost Sets dialogue boost to off, low, medium or high, here or on another device with Flexarr open. Play a podcast's latest episode The newest episode you haven't heard. What's new in my podcasts Says the newest episodes you haven't heard. Add a podcast to Up Next Puts the next episode at the end of Up Next. Play Up Next Plays your podcast queue from the start. Search Flexarr Opens the app on a search. In the next release, three more arrive with audiobooks: Resume listening, Play a book, and Sleep at the end of the chapter. The play and control actions have an On setting, where you choose this device or another one signed in to your server. That's handy for a shortcut of your own. A "Film night" shortcut could use Apple's own actions to dim the lights and wake the Apple TV, open Flexarr on it, then use Play a film or show with On set to that TV. Play a film or show and Shuffle a show also have an As setting, for the profile to watch as. The device switches to that profile first, so the next episode is that person's and what they watch lands in their Continue Watching, whoever used the TV last. A "Kids' bedtime episode" shortcut can play their show on the TV as their profile. If the profile has a PIN, the device asks for it before playing. Tip A shortcut you make can have a phrase of its own. Name it, and Siri runs it when you say that name. #Links Flexarr's links open the app on the iPhone, iPad or Apple TV they're opened on. Use them with Shortcuts' Open URLs action, an NFC tag or Home Assistant: Link What it does flexarr://item/<id> Shows a title's page. flexarr://play/<id> Plays a film or episode, or a show's next episode. Add ?t=<seconds> to start at a time, or ?shuffle=1 to shuffle a show. Add profile=<name> (or the profile's id) to either to switch to that profile first, for example flexarr://play/<id>?profile=Sam. If the profile has a PIN, Flexarr asks for it before going on. A title's id is the last part of its address on the web, after /item/. #If Siri doesn't understand "Open Flexarr and connect it to your server first." The app on this device isn't signed in. Open it and connect. See Connect your devices. "Nothing in your library is called …" Siri didn't recognise the title. Try saying it the way it's written in Flexarr. Siri learns titles when the app loads your profile, so open Flexarr once after adding something new. "… isn't signed in to the server any more." The device chosen in Settings › Siri was signed out. Choose another. Siri opens a different app. Make sure "Flexarr" is in the phrase. Siri works on what the profile chosen on that iPhone or iPad sees: its libraries, its next episodes and its podcasts, within any age limit. See Profiles.

title: Notifications and widgets
description: Get told on your iPhone or iPad when something new is ready, add Flexarr's widgets to your Home Screen, and fill the Apple TV's Top Shelf.
headings: What you can be told about
How they reach your phone, and what's shared
text: Flexarr can tell your phone when something new arrives, keep podcasts and your watchlist on your Home Screen and Lock Screen, and put what you're watching at the top of the Apple TV's Home screen. #Notifications (iPhone and iPad) #Turn them on In the Flexarr app, go to Settings › Notifications. Turn on Notifications, and allow them when iOS asks. Under Tell me about, choose what you want to hear about. Tap Send test notification to check one arrives. If iOS has notifications switched off for Flexarr, the page says so and offers Open Settings to allow them there first. #What you can be told about Films and Shows: something new in the library that you haven't seen, in a library your profile can see. A brand-new show says so, and several episodes of one show arriving together are one notification. Upgrades and replacements of things you already have don't count. Podcasts: a new episode of a show you follow. Recordings: a Live TV recording has finished. This appears when Live TV is set up. Requests: something you asked for through Flexarr is ready, or a title on your watchlist has arrived (From your watchlist). This takes the place of the ordinary "new" notification for it. In the next release, a book you asked for says it's ready to listen. Upcoming (off to start with): each morning, at the hour you choose under At, what's airing or out today from the shows you watch and the films you asked for. Phones on the main profile also hear, whatever they've chosen, when a device asks to connect (with Allow and Don't allow buttons: press and hold the notification) and when wrong guesses at the admin PIN lock someone out, naming the device. A library's first scan never notifies, and a big batch arriving at once is summed up in one notification, so adding a new library or a season pack won't flood your phone. Notifications have buttons. Films and episodes have Play, Download and Play on Apple TV. Podcast episodes have Play and Download. Tapping the notification opens the title. #One profile per phone Each phone gets notifications for one profile: the one it was on when you turned them on. A phone the household shares gets one set, not one for each person. If you switch profile, Settings › Notifications offers Get notifications for … instead. See Profiles. While child lock is on, the phone's notifications follow it to the kids profile, and go back when child lock is turned off. Signing the phone out, or signing it out from Settings › Security on the web, stops its notifications. #How they reach your phone, and what's shared Apple only delivers notifications that come from the app maker's own key, and that key can't be handed to every Flexarr server. So your server sends each notification through a small relay at push.flexarr.io, which hands it to Apple to deliver. Here's what goes where: When you turn notifications on, your phone makes a random secret key and gives it to your own server. It never leaves the two of them. When something new arrives, your server writes the notification (title, text, artwork link and buttons) and encrypts it with that key. Your server sends the relay the encrypted notification and your phone's Apple push address. The relay can't read the notification, and keeps nothing. The relay passes it to Apple under a plain "Something new is ready" message. On your phone, Flexarr decrypts it and shows the real title, text, artwork and buttons. So the relay and Apple see that your phone got a notification, and when, but not what it says. Artwork in a notification is a public poster address, which your phone fetches to show it. The one exception is the Lock Screen panel for a TV you're following. Apple reads its updates directly, so they can't be encrypted: they carry only whether the TV is paused, how far in it is, how long it is and its speed. The title and picture are put there by your phone and never pass through the relay. The privacy policy has the details. Note A server can use no relay at all. Set the environment variable Flexarr__Notifications__Enabled=false (or Flexarr:Notifications:Enabled set to false in the server's settings) and restart. The app then says your server has notifications turned off. #Widgets (iPhone and iPad) Flexarr has three widgets. Add them the usual way: touch and hold an empty part of the Home Screen, tap Edit › Add Widget, and search for Flexarr. Continue listening shows the episode you're on (in the next release, or the audiobook), with a play and pause button. Small and medium sizes for the Home Screen, and a Lock Screen size too. Up Next shows the episodes waiting in your Up Next queue. Small and medium sizes. Watchlist shows what's on your watchlist and ready to watch. Tap it to open your watchlist, or, in the medium size, a poster to open that title. Small and medium sizes. On iPhone and iPad the widgets show what the app last saved, and update when your podcasts or watchlist change in the app; they don't fetch anything from your server themselves. See Podcasts for Up Next. #Top Shelf (Apple TV) Put Flexarr in the top row of the Apple TV's Home screen, and the Top Shelf above it shows your Continue Watching, with Recently Added below it. Select a title to open it in Flexarr, or press Play on the remote to carry on watching straight away. With nothing in either, it shows featured titles instead. To choose how it looks: In Flexarr on the Apple TV, open Settings › Home screen. Choose Posters, which fit more titles in, or Wide artwork, with each title's logo on it. Titles you've started show how far through you are. The Top Shelf follows the profile chosen on the Apple TV, and only shows its libraries. Tip To move Flexarr to the top row, highlight its icon on the Apple TV's Home screen, press and hold until it wobbles, move it up, then press the remote's centre to drop it.

title: Home Assistant
description: Add Flexarr to Home Assistant so every Apple TV, iPhone and iPad becomes a media player, and dim the lights when a film starts.
text: Home Assistant is a popular app for running your smart home yourself. Flexarr has an integration for it, so your home can react to what you're watching: lights down when a film starts, up again when the credits roll. The integration lives in its own repository, flexarr-home-assistant, and needs Flexarr 0.45.0 or later. #What you get A media player for each device. Every Apple TV, iPhone and iPad signed in to Flexarr appears in Home Assistant, named as it is in Flexarr's list of signed-in devices. It shows what's playing (title, show, season and episode, artwork and position) and has play, pause and stop. It's idle while Flexarr is open with nothing playing, and off when Flexarr isn't open on it. Devices you connect later appear by themselves. Device triggers for started, paused, resumed, credits, ended and stopped, to pick in an automation's Device trigger. A flexarr_playback event for every change, which covers browsers too. #Install it The easiest way is through HACS, the community store for Home Assistant, which also tells you about updates. In Home Assistant, open HACS, then the ⋮ menu, then Custom repositories. Add https://github.com/danleach-glitch/flexarr-home-assistant with the type Integration. Find Flexarr in HACS, download it, and restart Home Assistant. Go to Settings › Devices & services › Add integration and choose Flexarr. Enter the Server address, for example http://192.168.1.20:8383, and the API key. The API key is in Flexarr under Settings › Security, signed in as the main profile. Showing it asks for the admin PIN. Note If you copied the integration into custom_components by hand before it had its own repository, it keeps working. Remove the old copy and install it through HACS to get updates. #Play something from Home Assistant Call media_player.play_media with a Flexarr title's id. You'll find the id in the title's address in the web app. A show's id plays the episode that device's profile is up to. action: media_player.play_media target: entity_id: media_player.living_room_tv data: media_content_id: 01a17ab1-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 media_content_type: tvshow As with Siri, Flexarr has to be open on the device for it to play. #The playback event flexarr_playback carries: Field What it is type started, paused, resumed, credits, ended or stopped device_id the Home Assistant device (none for a browser) device_name the device or browser, as named in Flexarr profile whose profile is watching media_type movie, episode, music or podcast title, series_title, season, episode what's playing media_id its Flexarr id position, duration in seconds Credits fires where Flexarr has found the end credits, within about ten seconds of them starting. A title without credits found goes straight to ended. See Subtitles and skipping for how credits are found. A playback that stops reporting counts as stopped after two minutes, or fifteen if it was paused. #Example: lights down for films This dims the living room when a film starts on the living room TV, and brings the lights up at the credits or when you stop. automation: - alias: Lights down for a film triggers: - trigger: event event_type: flexarr_playback event_data: type: started media_type: movie device_name: Living room TV actions: - action: light.turn_on target: { entity_id: light.living_room } data: { brightness_pct: 10, transition: 5 } - alias: Lights up at the credits triggers: - trigger: event event_type: flexarr_playback event_data: { type: credits, device_name: Living room TV } - trigger: event event_type: flexarr_playback event_data: { type: stopped, device_name: Living room TV } actions: - action: light.turn_on target: { entity_id: light.living_room } data: { brightness_pct: 80, transition: 10 } Change Living room TV to your device's name in Flexarr, and light.living_room to your own light. Tip Leave out media_type: movie to dim the lights for episodes too, or add a profile to make it only happen when you're the one watching. #For other automation tools The integration is built on Flexarr's event stream, which anything else can use too. GET /api/v1/events on your server is a stream of server-sent events: one playback event, as JSON, for each change, with a keep-alive comment every twenty seconds. Because it shows what everyone is watching, it needs the API key, sent as an X-Api-Key header. curl -N -H "X-Api-Key: <your key>" http://<server>:8383/api/v1/events Important The API key gives full control of your server. Keep Home Assistant and anything else holding it on your home network or your tailnet. See Watch away from home.

title: Use an AI assistant
description: Connect Claude or another AI assistant to Flexarr over MCP, so it can search your library, see what's playing and play things on your TV.
text: Flexarr is an MCP server. MCP (the Model Context Protocol) is a standard way for AI assistants such as Claude to use other apps. Connect one to Flexarr and you can ask it things like "What am I in the middle of?", "Put the next Traitors on the living room TV" or "Queue the new Rest Is History episodes". #What an assistant can do Tool What it does search_library Finds films, shows and episodes by title. continue_watching What you're in the middle of, most recent first. next_up The episode to watch next in a show. list_devices The TVs, phones and tablets signed in, whether Flexarr is open on each, and what each is playing. now_playing Everything playing right now on every screen: which device, whose profile, what, and how far in. play_on_device Plays a title on a device. A show plays the episode you're up to; it can shuffle a show or start from the beginning. control_device Pauses, resumes or stops a device. set_device_sound Changes a device's dialogue boost, night mode or speakers, while Flexarr is open on it. mark_watched Marks a film or episode watched or unwatched; a show or season marks every episode. Unwatched also forgets how far in it was, taking it out of Continue Watching. remove_from_continue_watching Takes a film or episode out of Continue Watching without marking it watched. A show stays out until you play another episode of it. watchlist Your watchlist, with whether each title is ready to play, on its way, coming out later, or not available. add_to_watchlist Adds a film or show to your watchlist: one from your library, or any title by name (that needs Seerr). Says if it was requested too. remove_from_watchlist Takes a title off your watchlist. It doesn't cancel a request. podcasts The podcasts you follow, with how many episodes you haven't heard. new_podcast_episodes The newest episodes you haven't heard. podcast_up_next Your podcast Up Next queue. add_to_up_next Queues an episode, at the end or to play next. live_channels Live TV channels with what's on now and next. watch_channel_on_device Puts a channel on a device. record_programme Sets a programme, or every showing of a series, to record. recordings What's set to record, and what's been recorded. audiobooks_in_progress Next release. The books you're part way through, most recent first, with how far in. set_sleep_timer Next release. Stops what a device is playing after some minutes, or at the end of the book's chapter. In the next release, play_on_device also plays a book from where you left it, and mark_watched marks one finished. See Audiobooks. The Live TV tools are only useful once Live TV is set up. See Live TV. As with Siri, a device only plays what it's told while Flexarr is open on it. If it isn't, the command waits two minutes for Flexarr to be opened there, and the assistant is told so. The assistant acts as the main profile, since it signs in with the API key. Its Continue Watching, podcasts and marks are the main profile's. #What you'll need Your server's address, such as http://mini.local:8383 or http://192.168.1.20:8383. The MCP address is that with /api/v1/mcp on the end. The API key, from Settings › Security in Flexarr, signed in as the main profile. Showing it asks for the admin PIN. #Claude Code In a terminal, run: claude mcp add --transport http flexarr http://mini.local:8383/api/v1/mcp --header "X-Api-Key: <your key>" Change mini.local to your server's name or address, and <your key> to the API key. Then start Claude Code and ask it something about your library. #Other assistants Any MCP client that can connect to a server over HTTP (sometimes called "Streamable HTTP") and send a header can use Flexarr. Give it: URL: http://<server>:8383/api/v1/mcp Header: X-Api-Key with your API key The exact place to enter these differs from app to app, so check your assistant's own help for adding an MCP server. Some apps, including Claude Desktop's configuration file, only start MCP servers as local programs. For those, a small bridge program that forwards to an HTTP server, such as mcp-remote, can connect them to Flexarr's address with the header. Follow the bridge's own instructions; note that some bridges insist on https:// unless told otherwise. Note Assistants that connect from the vendor's cloud, rather than from your own computer, can't reach a server on your home network. Use an assistant that runs on a computer at home or on your tailnet. #Keep it safe Important The API key is full access to your server. Anything holding it can change settings, see what everyone watches and delete media through Sonarr and Radarr. Treat it like a password. Keep the assistant on your network. Use Flexarr's home address, or its Tailscale address away from home (see Watch away from home). Never put Flexarr on the internet over plain http:// to reach it from an assistant. Don't share configuration files that contain the key, or commit them to a code repository. Prefer the header. Flexarr also accepts the key in the address as ?apikey=, for tools that can't send headers, but addresses end up in logs and histories more easily. If the key leaks, choose Make a new key in Settings › Security. Everything using the old key stops working until you give it the new one. Check before it acts. An assistant can play, stop, mark things watched and set recordings. Most assistant apps ask before using a tool; leave that on if you'd rather approve each one.

title: Bring your history over from Plex
description: Copy what each person has watched, and where they stopped, from Plex Media Server into Flexarr, matched by file and without changing Plex.
text: If you've been using Plex Media Server, Flexarr can copy across what you've watched and where you stopped, so Continue Watching and the watched ticks pick up where you left off. Plex itself is never changed: Flexarr takes a private copy of Plex's database, reads it, and deletes the copy. #What comes over Watched films and episodes, with how many times each was played. Resume points for anything part-watched, so it shows in Continue Watching. Profile pictures, if you use Plex Home (a separate button, below). Each Plex user's history goes into the Flexarr profile you choose, so the household's histories stay apart. #What doesn't Music and audiobooks. Only films and episodes are brought over. Files Flexarr doesn't have. Titles are matched by the file on disk, not by name. If a file Plex knows about isn't in one of your Flexarr libraries, it's skipped and counted in the summary. Anything else in Plex: playlists, collections, ratings, server settings and users. Create profiles in Flexarr yourself (Profiles). #Before you start Flexarr reads Plex's database file, com.plexapp.plugins.library.db, so it has to be able to see it. Plex on the same computer. Flexarr looks in the usual places on a Mac, on Linux and on Windows, and normally finds it without help. The Mac app (coming to the Mac App Store) can't look by itself: choose Choose Plex's folder on the Mac… and pick the Plex Media Server folder in your Library's Application Support folder. Plex in Docker, or Flexarr in Docker. Make Plex's data folder visible to Flexarr, for example by mounting it into Flexarr's container read-only, then give Flexarr the full path to the database file when it asks. The file sits in Plex's data folder under Plug-in Support/Databases/. Plex on a different computer. Copy its Plug-in Support/Databases folder to the Flexarr machine and point Flexarr at the copied com.plexapp.plugins.library.db. Note Flexarr only accepts a path to a file named com.plexapp.plugins.library.db. It won't read any other file you point it at. Matching is by file path, so your libraries need to be set up in Flexarr first, with their scans finished. If Plex saw your media under different paths from Flexarr (common when one of them runs in Docker), add a path mapping in Settings › Connections › Media folders before importing; Flexarr applies the same mappings to Plex's paths. See Media paths. #Bring the history over You need the main profile, with settings unlocked. In the web app, open Settings › Libraries and choose Bring over from Plex. Flexarr says where it found Plex. If it says Plex wasn't found, type the full path to com.plexapp.plugins.library.db and choose Look there. Under Whose history, pick the Plex user. Each is listed with how many titles they've watched and how many are in progress. If you have more than one Flexarr profile, choose one under Into which Flexarr profile. It starts on the main profile. Choose Bring history over. When it's done, a summary says how many titles were matched, how many are now watched, and how many are ready to resume. It also says how many files Plex knows about that aren't in your Flexarr libraries. Repeat steps 3 to 5 for each person, picking their Plex user and their Flexarr profile each time. #Running it again is safe You can run the import as often as you like. For each title, the most recent viewing wins: if you've watched something in Flexarr since you last watched it in Plex, Flexarr keeps its own, and the summary tells you how many were left alone. Play counts never go down. This makes it easy to try Flexarr alongside Plex for a while and bring over whatever you've watched in Plex in the meantime. Tip If a lot of files come up as not matched, check your path mappings, then rescan the libraries and run the import again. #Profile pictures Under the import there's a Profile pictures panel (not in the Mac app). Use Plex profile pictures takes each Plex Home user's picture and puts it on the Flexarr profile with the same name, replacing any picture it has. Plex's owner is matched to the main profile if no profile shares their name. This step does go online: Flexarr reads Plex's own sign-in from its settings file and makes one request to plex.tv for the list of Home users and their pictures. The sign-in isn't stored. If Flexarr can't find the sign-in, Plex Media Server needs to be on this machine (or its data folder visible to Flexarr) and signed in to plex.tv. If a Plex user has no matching profile, the summary names them. Add a profile with that name in Settings › Profiles and run it again.

title: Library health
description: Find spare copies and the space they use, files that can't be read, standard-definition films and wrong matches, and fix them with Sonarr and Radarr.
text: Library health is a check-up for your films and TV. It shows what's wrong, how much space spare copies take, and a button to fix each problem, usually by asking Sonarr or Radarr to do the work. Open it in the web app from Settings › Libraries › Library health, as the main profile with settings unlocked. The Overview page in Settings links to it too. #The health score At the top is a score out of 100: the share of your films and episodes with nothing wrong. Next to it is a breakdown of what's affecting the rest, such as spare copies, unreadable files or missing artwork. Groups with nothing in them are left out, and a line underneath says what's all clear ("every title has a single copy", "every film has an HD copy"). #Spare copies Sometimes a film or episode ends up with more than one file: an upgrade that didn't replace the old one, or the same file in two folders. Spare copies lists each one, how many copies it has and how much space the spares use. The total you'd free is in the group's description. Remove spares on a title deletes its extra files. Remove all spare copies does the whole list, after asking first, with a progress bar. Flexarr always keeps two copies safe: the best one (highest quality), and the one Sonarr or Radarr are tracking. Usually they're the same file. When they're not, both stay and the summary tells you; open the title's row to see each copy with its resolution, codec and size, and use Delete this copy on the one you don't want. Copies that are the same file twice are marked Identical. Important Removing spares deletes files from your disk. It can't be undone. #Run a health check The Health check panel looks at every file: whether it's still on disk, whether it's empty, and whether it can be read. Choose Run health check and it works through your library in the background, with a progress bar. Problems are listed under Missing from disk, Empty files and Still unreadable, each with Search again to have Sonarr or Radarr fetch it again. #Files that can't be read Files Flexarr couldn't open when it scanned them are listed under Files that can't be read, with the reason. This is usually a damaged or unfinished download. Get a new copy asks Sonarr or Radarr to search for the title again; a fresh copy fixes playback. #Audible books From the next release, audiobooks bought from Audible as .aax or .aaxc files are listed here too, as protected by Audible's DRM. Flexarr can't play them. Convert them to .m4b with a tool that uses your own Audible account, put the .m4b in the book's folder in place of the original, and rescan. #Standard-definition films Only in standard definition lists films whose best copy is below 720p. Find a better copy asks Radarr to search for the film again, so it can upgrade it within the quality profile you've set in Radarr. When Sonarr or Radarr are already fetching a new copy, the row shows how far along it is ("Downloading 45%") instead of the button. #Check these matches Films and shows that Sonarr and Radarr don't manage get their details by searching for the folder's name. That can find the wrong title: an older show with the same name, or a remake. They're listed under Check these matches. If a match is right, choose Ignore. It leaves the list and stays as it is. If it's wrong, choose Fix match (below). #Missing artwork Titles with no poster or details are listed under Missing artwork. Artwork comes from .nfo files and pictures beside the title, from Radarr and Sonarr, from TVmaze for shows, and from TMDB for films if you've added a key. If Radarr and Sonarr aren't connected, connect them in Settings › Connections (Connect Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr and Seerr), or see Without Sonarr and Radarr. Otherwise the title wasn't found: fix its match, or rename its folder to the form Title (Year) and rescan. #Fix match Fix match puts right a film or show that's been matched to the wrong title. It's on each row in Check these matches and Missing artwork, and in the ⋯ menu on any film's or show's page (main profile only). Choose Fix match. The dialog shows the full path of the film's files, or the show's folder, so you can see what's being matched. Search for the right title. Try the title as it was first released, or add the year. Pick it. Each result says whether it's the Current match, already in Sonarr or Radarr, or would be added to them. Flexarr keeps your choice through every later refresh. If the title wasn't in Sonarr or Radarr, fixing the match adds it there using the folder it's already in, so they manage it from then on. Without Sonarr, the search is TVmaze's; without Radarr, it's TMDB's, which needs a TMDB key (see Without Sonarr and Radarr). Then your choice is kept in Flexarr, and nothing is added anywhere. Note If Sonarr or Radarr already use that folder for a different title, Flexarr won't change it for you. Remove that title in Sonarr or Radarr (keeping its files), then fix the match again. To undo a fix, open Fix match again and choose Match automatically again. #Deleting a title To delete a film, show or episode, open its page, then ⋯ › Delete… (main profile only). The dialog says who'll do the deleting before you confirm: A film Radarr manages: Radarr deletes the film's files from disk and stops tracking it. A show Sonarr manages: Sonarr deletes every episode's files and stops tracking the show. An episode: Sonarr deletes the episode's file and stops downloading it, so it doesn't come back. An audiobook (from the next release) that Readarr, Bookshelf or Chaptarr manage: it deletes the book's files and unmonitors the book there, so it isn't fetched again. A title neither manages: Flexarr deletes the video files itself and lists them first. It also removes folders left empty, but never a library's own folder or anything outside it. If Sonarr or Radarr can't be reached or refuse, nothing is removed from Flexarr either. Important Deleting can't be undone. Back up anything you want to keep first. #Folders on hold If a drive or network share isn't connected when Flexarr scans, its titles aren't removed; the folder is put on hold instead, and your watch history is kept. Held folders are listed in Library health with the reason, such as "The folder isn't there. Is its drive or share connected?". Reconnect the drive and the next scan carries on as normal. If you really did empty the folder on purpose, choose Confirm removal and its titles go.

title: Backups
description: How Flexarr backs itself up every night, where backups are kept, and how to restore one or move your settings to another server.
headings: Restore or import from a file
text: Your films, shows and music live on your own drives, and Flexarr can always scan them again. What it can't rebuild is everything you've added on top: profiles, what everyone has watched, watchlists, playlists, collections, settings and signed-in devices. That's what a backup holds. Everything here is in the web app under Settings › Backup & restore, as the main profile with settings unlocked. #What's in a backup Profiles, with their PINs and pictures, and the admin PIN What every profile has watched, and where they stopped Watchlists, playlists, collections, podcast follows and other per-profile data Each profile's Trakt connection The server's settings and keys (config.json) Signed-in browsers, phones and TVs Artwork, subtitles and scrubbing previews are left out. They come back by themselves. Your media files and logs aren't included either. #Automatic backups Flexarr makes a backup every night at half past three and keeps the last 7. If the server was off overnight, it catches up a few minutes after it next starts. It also makes one before an upgrade changes the database, and before a restore, so you can always go back. The last 3 of each of those are kept. Backups you make by hand are never deleted automatically. To stop the nightly backups, turn off Back up every night under Automatic backups. We don't recommend it. #Back up now Choose Back up now at any time, for example before changing a lot of settings. Each backup in the list shows when it was made, why (Nightly, Made by hand, Before an upgrade, Before a restore), its size and the Flexarr version. #Where backups are kept The list says where: Kept in and the folder. By default that's a backups folder inside Flexarr's data folder: Install Default backups folder Mac ~/.flexarr/data/backups Docker /config/backups inside the container, so wherever you mapped /config A backup on the same drive as Flexarr won't help if that drive fails. To keep them elsewhere, type another folder under Automatic backups › Folder and choose Save: a second drive, or a network share mounted on the server. In Docker, the folder has to be one you've mapped into the container. Leave it empty to go back to the data folder. If the chosen folder isn't there when a backup is due (a drive that's unplugged, or a share that didn't mount), Flexarr says so on the page rather than quietly filling up its own drive. #Download a backup Use the Download icon on a backup to save a copy to your computer. You can protect it with a passphrase of at least 8 characters. The file holds your server's keys and the passwords for Sonarr, Radarr and the like, so either set a passphrase or keep the file somewhere private. Tip Flexarr asks for the passphrase when you open the file later. Keep it in a password manager. #Restore a backup Restoring puts the whole server back to how it was when the backup was made: profiles, what's been watched, and all your settings, keys and sign-ins. Anything since is lost. Find the backup in the list and use its Restore icon. To restore a file you downloaded, use From a file further down the page instead (below). Read the warning, and enter the admin PIN. Choose Restore and restart. Flexarr first makes a copy of the server as it is now (it appears in the list as Before a restore), so you can change your mind. It then restarts to put the backup in place. Anyone watching is stopped. The page reloads when Flexarr is back. Before anything changes, the backup is checked. A damaged one, one made by a newer version of Flexarr, or a file that isn't a Flexarr backup is refused. This machine's own paths (ffmpeg and the cache) are kept as they are. Important Flexarr stops itself to finish a restore and relies on whatever runs it to start it again. The Mac install does this. In Docker, the container needs a restart policy such as --restart unless-stopped (or restart: unless-stopped in Compose). Without one, start the container again by hand within the hour, or the restore is dropped. #Restore or import from a file From a file takes either a downloaded backup or a settings file (below), from this server or another. Choose Choose a file… and pick the file. If it's protected, enter its passphrase and choose Open. Flexarr shows what's inside: when it was made, by which version, and how many profiles, libraries and titles it holds. For a backup, choose Restore… and carry on as above. If the backup came from a different Flexarr server, Flexarr points this out. Restoring it brings that server's keys and its signed-in browsers and devices, so only restore one you made yourself. #Moving to another server Two ways, depending on what you want to take: Everything, history included: download a backup on the old server and restore it on the new one with From a file. Mount your media at the same paths on the new machine, or fix up the library folders afterwards in Settings › Libraries. Settings only: use Export… under Settings file on the old server, then From a file on the new one. A settings file holds libraries and the server's settings, without profiles, watch history or Trakt connections. When you import a settings file, you choose which parts to take: Libraries, Connections (Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Seerr, Bazarr, the TMDB key, your own Trakt app and path mappings), Live TV, Streaming, Home & browse (for profiles that haven't chosen their own rows), Podcasts, Notifications, Access, This machine's paths and Server keys. Each library's folders can be changed to where they are on the new machine. This machine's paths and Server keys start unticked, and taking either of them, or Access, asks for the admin PIN. Log and update settings, and the admin PIN, aren't in a settings file: the new server keeps its own. Nor are profiles, so each profile's own Home & browse and menu choices move only with a full backup. See also Updating, which makes its own backup before any upgrade that changes the database.

title: Logs and diagnostics
description: Read Flexarr's log, turn up the detail for one area, follow a single playback, collect diagnostics from the apps, and choose whether to send error reports.
text: Flexarr keeps a log of what the server and its apps do. When a film won't play, a scan stalls or Sonarr can't be reached, the log usually says why. It stays on your server: nothing in it is sent anywhere unless you download it and send it yourself. #Reading the log Open Settings › Logs in the web app, as the main profile with settings unlocked. The newest entries are at the top. Select an entry to see its details. To narrow it down: Minimum level: show only warnings and errors, say, or everything down to Debug. Area: one part of Flexarr, such as Playback or Library scans, or All areas. Search: any text in the entry. Live: turn it on to watch new entries arrive as they happen. It's handy while you reproduce a problem. Load older at the bottom goes further back. #Following one playback Every time something starts playing it gets a short id, such as 3f9a1c07. The server's lines about that playback show it as #3f9a1c07, and the Apple TV, iPhone and iPad apps attach the same id to what they report. Open an entry and select its playbackId to see only that playback: the whole story, from the server and the device, from start to finish. #Turning up the detail Under Levels, the Default level applies to the whole server. Each area can be set to log more (Debug) or less (Warning) than that. Changes apply straight away, with no restart. Area What it covers General Everything not below, including startup Playback Direct play, transcoding, ffmpeg, downloads to phones Library scans Scanning, reading files, imports Sonarr, Radarr, Seerr and Bazarr Calls to the *arr apps, Seerr and Bazarr Metadata and artwork TVmaze, TMDB, artwork Live TV Dispatcharr channels, the guide, recordings Podcasts Feeds and episode downloads Notifications Push notifications Web requests One line per request. Failures show at Information; set Debug to see every request Apps and browsers What the apps and browsers report Tip Chasing a problem? Set its area to Debug, make the problem happen again, then set the area back to Default so the log doesn't fill up. #What the apps send Automatically: warnings and errors from the Apple TV, iPhone and iPad apps, and errors from the web app. They appear under the Apps and browsers area, named after the device. When you ask: Send diagnostics sends a device's recent log in full. On Apple TV, iPhone and iPad it's in the app's Settings › Server › Send diagnostics. Add a note saying what happened and roughly when, then send. Diagnostics go to your server and nowhere else. They're listed under Diagnostics from apps at the bottom of the Logs page, with the device, app version, profile and when they arrived, and a Download button for each. #Download diagnostics Download diagnostics, at the top of the Logs page, makes a zip for looking into a problem. It holds: the server's logs, with titles, file names, device names and IP addresses in them diagnostics sent from the apps your settings (config.json), with every key and password blanked but the addresses of Sonarr, Radarr and your other connections, your path mappings and the server's known host names left in a description of the server: Flexarr version, operating system, ffmpeg, free space, your libraries' names and how many titles, files and profiles there are So it says a lot about your home network and your library. Send it privately to whoever is helping you, rather than attaching it to a public GitHub issue. #What's taken out API keys, passwords, sign-in tokens and playback session ids are removed before anything is written: keys and passwords become ***, and long tokens become a short #id. That's true of the server's log files, what the apps send and the diagnostics zip. Everything else stays, including titles, file names and addresses, because they're what you need to work out what went wrong. #How long logs are kept Logs are kept for 14 days, and the log folder is capped at 100 MB, oldest files first. Change both under Retention on the Logs page: Keep for (days) and Largest size (MB). The server starts a new file each day (flexarr-20261027.log, say), and another if one day's passes 10 MB. Each line is a JSON object, so other tools can read them. Install Log folder Mac ~/.flexarr/logs (in the Mac app, coming to the Mac App Store: Show Logs in its menu) Docker /config/logs (and docker logs flexarr) Anywhere else logs in Flexarr's data folder, or set Flexarr__Logs__Directory #Error reports You can choose to send error reports to Flexarr's developer, so bugs get found and fixed sooner. It's off unless you turn it on. The switch, Send error reports to Flexarr's developer, is at the top of the Logs page. One switch covers the server and every app and browser connected to it, and turning it off stops it everywhere at once. What's sent, and what never is opens the full list. Sent, only when something goes wrong: what went wrong and where in Flexarr's code, the Flexarr version, the operating system and device model, and a random id for your server that isn't linked to you. Never sent: titles, file names or paths, what anyone watches, your logs, profile and device names, addresses (IP, server, network), keys and passwords. Reports are cleaned on your server or device before they leave it, and one that can't be cleaned isn't sent. They go to Sentry, which stores them in the EU and deletes them after at most 90 days. See also Troubleshooting, which starts most fixes from this page.

title: Troubleshooting
description: Fixes for the most common Flexarr problems, from an app that can't find your server to playback that won't start, HDR, sound and connecting away from home.
headings: The app can't find my server
The app says the server hasn't been set up
I can't connect away from home
HDR looks washed out or dim
No sound, or Dolby Atmos is missing
The Apple TV app stopped opening after 7 days
text: Most problems have a short fix. Find yours below. If it isn't here, or the fix doesn't work, the log usually says what's wrong: see Logs and diagnostics, and where to get help at the end. #Connecting #The app can't find my server The iPhone, iPad and Apple TV apps look for Flexarr on your home Wi-Fi. If Looking for Flexarr… never finds it: Check the server is running. On another device on the same network, open http://<server>:8383 in a browser, using the computer's name or IP address. If that doesn't load, the problem is the server, not the app. See your install guide: Mac, Synology, Unraid or Docker. Check you're on the same network. The device must be on the same Wi-Fi as the server, not a guest network and not mobile data. Check local network access (iPhone and iPad). The app asks to find devices on your local network the first time it opens. If you said no, turn it back on in the iPhone's Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network › Flexarr. Type the address instead. Choose Enter its address on iPhone and iPad, or Enter an address instead on Apple TV, and type the address that worked in the browser, such as http://192.168.1.20:8383. You'll still get a code to approve. If the browser test works but discovery doesn't, your router may block devices from announcing themselves to each other. Typing the address always works. #The app says the server hasn't been set up A new Flexarr server has no owner until someone sets it up in a browser. The app shows the steps; here they are in full: On a computer on your home network, open the server's address (the app shows it) in a web browser. Enter the server's setup code (it's in the server's log; First setup says where for your install) and choose Set up Flexarr. That browser becomes the server's owner, with no key needed. Go to Settings › Security › Connect a device and type in the code the app is showing. The app moves on by itself once you have. See First setup. Set up Flexarr only appears to a browser on your home network, using the server's own name or IP address. It won't appear over the internet, or once someone has set the server up. If someone else in the house set it up, ask them to approve your code from their browser. #I can't connect away from home Flexarr isn't on the public internet. Away from home, the apps reach it over Tailscale. Check each of these: Remote access is on. In the web app, Settings › Remote access › Away from home should say On: Flexarr is available on your tailnet. If it says Tailscale isn't installed or isn't connected, install Tailscale on the server and sign in first. (Docker can't use Tailscale: see Away from home.) Tailscale is connected on your phone or tablet, signed in to the same tailnet. You have a profile. If people use their own Tailscale accounts, each one needs a profile under People with their own Tailscale. Anyone set to Not allowed is turned away. The app has picked up the address. It learns the Tailscale address from the server and uses it when the home address can't be reached. If remote access was turned on after the app connected, close and reopen the app at home once. In the app, Settings › Server shows both addresses and which one it's using. Full details are in Away from home. #Your library #New downloads don't appear Flexarr rescans each library every 12 hours, and straight away when Sonarr, Radarr or Lidarr tell it something's arrived. Connecting one of them in Flexarr adds that webhook to it for you. If new downloads take hours to show up, the webhook is missing or failing: add it by hand. In Flexarr, open Settings › Connections and find Webhooks. Copy the address for each app. In Sonarr (and Radarr, and Lidarr), go to Settings › Connect › + › Webhook, paste the address, set the method to POST, and tick On Import, On Upgrade, On Rename and On Delete. Use Test in Sonarr to check it gets through. If Sonarr runs in Docker on the same computer as Flexarr, use host.docker.internal in the address in place of the computer's name. If you made a new webhook secret in Flexarr, the old addresses stop working: copy the new ones in. If the webhook arrives but nothing appears, the paths probably don't match. Sonarr tells Flexarr the folder by its own path, such as /data/tv/Show, and Flexarr has to see the same folder at that path. Either mount your media at the same path in both, or check Settings › Connections › Media folders: an amber line there is a folder Flexarr hasn't found yet, with a suggestion or a folder to choose. See Media paths. To pick something up now, use the Scan for new and changed files icon on the library in Settings › Libraries. #Artwork or details are missing Films and shows get their artwork and details from .nfo files and pictures beside them first, then from Radarr and Sonarr. Shows they don't know are looked up on TVmaze, and films on TMDB if you've added a TMDB key. Are they connected? Check Settings › Connections. Without Sonarr and Radarr, a film needs a TMDB key (or its own .nfo and poster) to get artwork. See Without Sonarr and Radarr. Is it the wrong title? Open Settings › Libraries › Library health and look under Missing artwork and Check these matches. Use Fix match to pick the right one. See Library health. Is the folder named clearly? For titles Sonarr and Radarr don't manage, Flexarr searches by the folder's name. Title (Year) works best, or an .nfo with the title's IDs. Refresh it. In Settings › Libraries, use Refresh artwork and details on the library. For music, artist pictures and album covers come from Lidarr when it's connected, otherwise from the artwork in each album's folder and the files' tags. #Watching #Playback buffers or won't start First, look at what the player says it's doing. The Apple TV, iPhone and iPad players show in a corner whether you're watching the original or a converted stream. Converting takes work on the server; the original takes almost none. "The server is busy." Flexarr converts up to 3 videos at once by default, so a busy evening can fill it. Wait for another screen to finish, or see How many streams at once?. Turn on Play files directly (Apple TV, iPhone and iPad, in the app's Settings › Playback). It's on by default. The device plays the file itself, so the server only sends bytes. Check hardware acceleration. In the web app, Settings › Streaming › Hardware acceleration should normally be Automatic (recommended); the list only offers what this server's ffmpeg supports. Converting on the graphics chip is far quicker than on the processor. On a Mac, run Flexarr natively rather than in Docker, which can't use the Mac's hardware. In Docker on Linux, the graphics device (usually /dev/dri) has to be passed into the container for Intel or AMD graphics. See Playback and transcoding. Check the network. Wi-Fi a long way from the router struggles with 4K. A cable to the Apple TV helps most. Away from home, set Limit each stream to in Settings › Streaming: 4 Mbps suits most connections. Check the file. If one title fails and others play, the file may be damaged. Run health check in Library health, then Search again. If it still won't play, set the Playback area to Debug in Settings › Logs, try again, and look for that playback's id. See Logs and diagnostics. #HDR looks washed out or dim On Apple TV, turn on Match Content. In the Apple TV's own Settings › Video and Audio › Match Content, turn on Match Dynamic Range. Flexarr's player then asks the TV to switch to HDR or Dolby Vision for titles that have it, and back for ones that don't. Leave Play files directly on, so HDR10, HLG and Dolby Vision reach the TV untouched. In a web browser, HDR films are converted to standard dynamic range so they look right on any screen. For HDR, watch on the Apple TV. More in HDR and Dolby Atmos. #No sound, or Dolby Atmos is missing No sound at all, on Apple TV with a receiver or soundbar: try turning off Lossless surround in the app's Settings › Playback. With it on, TrueHD and DTS-HD soundtracks go as multichannel PCM, which some soundbars and receivers don't accept. Off, they go as Dolby Digital Plus, which anything plays. Atmos: Dolby Atmos in Dolby Digital Plus reaches the Apple TV, iPhone and iPad intact. Atmos inside TrueHD doesn't yet keep its height channels; it's on the roadmap. The web player doesn't pass Atmos through. Dialogue boost, Night mode or Speakers turn Atmos into plain surround while any of them is on. Turn them off (and Speakers to Auto) in the player's audio menu or Settings › Playback for the full Atmos. Away from home with a stream limit, the sound is compressed to save data. More in HDR and Dolby Atmos. #Apps and profiles #The Apple TV app stopped opening after 7 days The Apple TV app is with Apple for review. Until it's on the App Store, it installs from Xcode. With a free Apple ID, Apple only lets apps installed that way run for 7 days. Run the install command again to refresh it: make apple-install TEAM=<your team id> BUNDLE_ID=com.yourname.flexarr.tv With a paid Apple Developer account, an install lasts a year instead. See Apple TV with Xcode. #I forgot a profile's PIN Someone else's profile: choose Forgot PIN? under its PIN pad and enter the admin PIN, which takes the PIN off. Or sign in as the main profile, open Settings › Profiles, edit their profile, and set a new PIN or remove it. You don't need the old one. The main profile's own PIN: the admin PIN opens the main profile too. Then set a new one or remove it in Settings › Profiles, as for anyone. The admin PIN: in a browser, open Settings, choose Forgotten it? under the PIN (or Change then Use the API key instead in Settings › Security), and enter the server's API key with a new PIN. That browser is unlocked, and anywhere the old PIN was given is locked again. The Apple TV and phone apps send you to a browser for this. The Mac app: choose Reset Admin PIN… from Flexarr's menu bar icon and type a new PIN. Being at the Mac is enough; no key is needed. The API key is in Flexarr's config.json: ~/.flexarr/data/config.json on a Mac, or /config/config.json in Docker. After a few wrong PINs, the profile is locked on that device for a while, longer each time. Other devices aren't affected. #Getting help #Where can I get help? Open an issue on GitHub: github.com/danleach-glitch/flexarr/issues. To help us fix it quickly: Say what you did, what you expected, and what happened instead. Include your Flexarr version (Settings › About) and the device and app you were using. If it happened on an Apple TV, iPhone or iPad, use Send diagnostics in the app's Settings › Server right after it happens, with a short note. In the web app, open Settings › Logs and choose Download diagnostics. Don't attach it to the issue: paste in the log lines that show the problem, and say you can send the zip privately if it's needed. Keys and passwords are taken out of the zip, but your titles, file names and addresses stay in, so it doesn't belong on a public page. See Logs and diagnostics. Ideas and feature requests go in Discussions.

text: #The basics #What is Flexarr? Flexarr is a media server you run yourself, on a computer at home. It organises your films, TV, home videos, music and podcasts, and live TV from an IPTV source, and plays them on the web, Apple TV, iPhone and iPad. Audiobooks arrive in the next release. There's no Flexarr account and no cloud service in the middle: your library and everything about it stays on your server. It's built to sit alongside Sonarr, Radarr and Lidarr, which fetch and organise your media, and Seerr, which handles requests. #Is it free? Yes. The server and the apps are free, with no subscription and no adverts. Flexarr is licensed under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0. You can use it, change it and share it for any noncommercial purpose: at home, for yourself and your family, or in a charity, school or other noncommercial organisation. You can't sell it or use it in a commercial product or service without a separate licence from the author. Because it restricts commercial use, Flexarr is source-available rather than open source in the Open Source Initiative's sense. The source code is all on GitHub. If you'd like to support it, see flexarr.io/donate. #Do I need Sonarr, Radarr or Lidarr? Flexarr works best with them, and they're where most of its information comes from. Here's what each one adds: Sonarr and Radarr supply the posters, artwork and details for your shows and films, with no extra accounts or API keys. Without them, Flexarr still finds and plays your video files, and takes artwork and details from any .nfo files and images beside them (as Kodi, Jellyfin and Plex users often have), from TVmaze for shows, and from TMDB for films with a free key of your own. See Without Sonarr and Radarr. They also power Coming soon, deleting through Sonarr and Radarr, and "find a better copy" in Library health. Lidarr supplies artist pictures, album covers and the split into albums, EPs and singles. Music works without it, using the tags in your files and any artwork in their folders. Seerr lets you request films and shows from Discover. Without it, Discover shows your own library by genre. Bazarr finds subtitles from the player when a title has none in your language. Cast and crew for TV shows come from TVmaze, which needs no setup. Podcasts are built in and need none of these apps. See Connect Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr and Seerr. #What hardware do I need? Any computer that stays on at home and can see your media: A Mac, Apple silicon or Intel. Flexarr runs natively, and uses the Mac's graphics chip to convert video when a device needs it. See Install on a Mac. A NAS or Linux machine with Docker. The image runs on Intel/AMD (x86-64) and ARM (arm64) machines. See Synology, Unraid and Docker. Most of the time the server does very little: the Apple TV, iPhone and iPad play files as they are, and the server sends the bytes. It works harder when it has to convert a video for a device that can't play it, such as a web browser with a 4K HEVC film. A graphics chip that can do this (Apple's VideoToolbox, Intel Quick Sync, VA-API or NVIDIA NVENC) makes a big difference. The apps need iOS, iPadOS or tvOS 18.2 or later. More in What you need. #Using it #Can several people use it? Yes. Each person gets a profile with their own Continue Watching, watched history, watchlist, playlists, podcasts and settings, which follow them from device to device. Profiles can have a PIN, an age limit, and be kept out of particular libraries; kids profiles see only what suits them. A shared Apple TV can ask who's watching each time Flexarr opens. The main profile manages the server, with an admin PIN guarding its settings; the others can change their own playback and podcast settings. See Profiles. #How many people can watch at once? Flexarr doesn't limit how many screens play at once. In practice the limit is your server and your network. Files played as they are (most playback on Apple TV, iPhone and iPad) take very little work, so many can run at once. Converted streams take real work. Flexarr converts up to 3 videos at once by default, which suits a Mac mini. When that's full, the next person to start one is told the server is busy, and one profile can't take every slot. You can change the number with maxConcurrentTranscodes under transcoding in config.json (0 means no limit), then restart Flexarr. Live TV is limited by how many connections your IPTV provider allows, though everyone watching the same channel shares one. #Does it work away from home? Yes, through Tailscale, a free service that links your own devices privately. Nothing is opened on your router, and Flexarr isn't put on the public internet. Once remote access is on, the apps switch to it by themselves when you leave home, and back again when you return. You can share it by inviting someone to your tailnet and giving them a profile. If you'd rather use your own HTTPS reverse proxy, that works too. See Away from home. #Can I watch offline? On iPhone and iPad, yes: download films, episodes, albums, playlists and podcast episodes. What you watch offline counts once you're back online. See Downloads. #Privacy #Does any data leave my home? Your library, what everyone watches, your profiles and your logs stay on your server. Flexarr has no account, analytics or adverts. A few things do go out, each for a reason: Artwork and details. The server downloads posters and artwork from the image addresses Sonarr, Radarr and Lidarr give it, looks up shows on TVmaze, and films on TMDB if you add a TMDB key. Audiobook details (from the next release) come from Audible and Open Library, and from Google Books and Hardcover if you add their keys. Updates. Once a day the server asks GitHub whether there's a newer version. Trakt, if a profile connects to it. Signing in goes through the relay at push.flexarr.io unless you use your own Trakt app. Podcasts. Browsing and search use Apple's podcast directory, and the server fetches each show's feed and episodes. Your devices play them through your server, so podcast hosts see your server rather than each listener. Live TV logos, if you use Live TV, come from a community collection on GitHub. Notifications, if you turn them on, pass through a small relay at push.flexarr.io on their way to Apple. They're encrypted on your server so only your phone can read them; the relay never sees what's in them and keeps nothing. The iPhone's Lock Screen panel for a TV is the exception: its updates carry only whether it's paused, how far in it is, how long it is and its speed, unencrypted, never the title or picture. Error reports, only if you turn them on. They describe what went wrong in Flexarr's code, with titles, names, addresses and keys removed first. See Logs and diagnostics. Plex profile pictures, only if you use that button, make one request to plex.tv. See Bring your history over from Plex. The apps talk only to your server. The full details are in the privacy policy. #Apps #Is there an Apple TV app on the App Store? Not yet: it's with Apple for review. The iPhone and iPad app is on the App Store. Until the Apple TV app joins it, you can install it on your own Apple TV from a Mac with Xcode. See Apple TV with Xcode. #Is there an Android app? Android and Android TV apps are on the way: see flexarr.io/apps. Until then, the web app works in your phone's browser. #Is there a Mac app? Flexarr Server for Mac is coming to the Mac App Store. Until then, you can build the server on your Mac from source: see Install on a Mac. #Does it do photos? Not yet. #Which languages does it speak? English only, for now. #Does it work with Siri? On iPhone and iPad, yes: "Play the next episode of Curb Your Enthusiasm in Flexarr", "Shuffle Family Guy in Flexarr", and podcast commands too. See Siri and Shortcuts. #Getting help #Where do I report a bug? On GitHub: github.com/danleach-glitch/flexarr/issues. Say what happened and what you expected. Don't attach the zip from Download diagnostics to a public issue: it holds your addresses and file names. See Troubleshooting. #Where do I ask for a feature? In Ideas on GitHub Discussions. The roadmap links each planned feature to its discussion, so you can add your vote and thoughts there. #What's changed in each version? Settings › Updates in the web app shows your version and what's new in the latest one, and the full changelog is on GitHub. To upgrade, see Updating.
